cues.zh: 但没有什么是完美的。

cues.en: One of the downsides is the entire database, and by database in this case, I mean cluster.
cues.zh: 缺点之一是整个数据库，这里说的数据库指的是集群。

cues.en: You have to replicate the entire thing or none of it. Every single thing has to be replicated.
cues.zh: 你要么复制全部，要么一点都不复制。每一样东西都必须被复制。

cues.en: So you can't pick a particular database, you can't pick a particular set of tables,
cues.zh: 所以你没法挑某个特定的数据库，也没法挑某组特定的表，

cues.en: the whole thing gets replicated.
cues.zh: 整个东西都会被复制。

cues.en: The secondary can't take rights of any kind, and it's very... Postgres is very strict about what in... What a right includes. For example, creating a temporary table is a right, and you can't do that on the secondary.
cues.zh: 从库无法接收任何写入，而且非常……Postgres 对写入具体包含什么非常严格。例如，创建临时表就算一种写入，你在从库上就做不了。

cues.en: So there's a lot of stuff you can't do on the secondary.
cues.zh: 所以很多操作在从库上都无法执行。

cues.en: There are certain things that aren't replicated.
cues.zh: 还有一些内容是不会被复制的。

cues.en: Temporary tables on the primary aren't replicated.
cues.zh: 主库上的临时表不会被复制。

cues.en: Unlogged tables, a relatively
cues.zh: 非日志表（unlogged tables），这是一个相对

cues.en: obscure Postgres feature,
cues.zh: 冷门的 Postgres 特性，

cues.en: replicated.
cues.zh: 也不会被复制。

cues.en: So
cues.zh: 所以

cues.en: my advice is to start with WALL E. Just play with it, get it set up.
cues.zh: 我的建议是从 WAL-E 入手。先上手玩玩，把它配置好。

cues.en: The README tells you everything you need to know about how to set it up.
cues.zh: README 里讲清楚了配置所需的一切。

cues.en: One of the nice parts about WALL E is there are a large number of really complex
cues.zh: WAL-E 的一大优势在于，面对许多非常复杂的

cues.en: replication situations,
cues.zh: 复制场景，

cues.en: like having one primary and multiple secondaries using
cues.zh: 比如一主多从架构下使用

cues.en: wall shipping...
cues.zh: WAL 传送……

cues.en: Wall archiving,
cues.zh: WAL 归档，

cues.en: and WALL E just handles all those for you. So that's really nice.
cues.zh: WAL-E 都能直接帮你搞定。这真的很棒。

cues.en: And even if you decide this is not where you wanna go, ultimately, if you scale out of it or something like that, you... It's a good way of educating yourself on the concepts behind
cues.zh: 就算你最终觉得这不适合你，比如规模超出其承载能力等等，你……这也不失为一个好方法，能帮你搞懂背后的

cues.en: behind what's going on there.
cues.zh: 底层运行概念。

cues.en: Okay.
cues.zh: 好的。

cues.en: Now for those cases where you say, well, okay, that's all very great, but we can't accept the limitations. For example, we need our secondary to be writable,
cues.zh: 现在，遇到这种情况时，你可能会说：好吧，这些都很好，但我们没法接受这些限制。比如，我们需要让备用库可写，

cues.en: or we only want to replicate a subset of the total data.
cues.zh: 或者我们只想复制全部数据中的一部分。

cues.en: The traditional way of doing this in Postgres is a class of tools called trigger based replication.
cues.zh: 在 Postgres 里，传统做法是使用一类叫作基于触发器的复制工具。

cues.en: The way... These these all work by installing triggers on the primary,
cues.zh: 这些工具的工作方式是：在主库上安装触发器，

cues.en: and then a daemon process... And these trigger... Triggers fire every time there's a change on the primary.
cues.zh: 然后由一个守护进程……这些触发器会在主库每次发生变更时触发。

cues.en: The stuff gets squirreled away in some kind of archive table, and then the daemon process comes and drains the archive table and applies them.
cues.zh: 这些东西会被暂存到某种归档表里，然后守护进程会来清空归档表并应用它们。

cues.en: These are all, right now, third party add ons to Postgres.
cues.zh: 目前这些都是 Postgres 的第三方扩展。

cues.en: None of these are core tools.
cues.zh: 这些都不是核心工具。

cues.en: The good part about these are these are really configurable.
cues.zh: 它们的好处是非常灵活，可配置性很强。

cues.en: You can push all our parts of tables. You can have exotic topologies of cascading and things like that. Streaming replication can also cascade.
cues.zh: 你可以推送表的各个部分，也可以设置各种复杂的级联拓扑之类的。流复制也可以级联。

cues.en: Now
cues.zh: 现在

cues.en: you can... And because it's these... Each individual node is just a standard Postgres database,
cues.zh: 你可以……因为正是这些……每个单独的节点只是一个标准的 Postgres 数据库，

cues.en: individual nodes can be writable as well.
cues.zh: 单独的节点也可以是可写的。

cues.en: You can also do multi master where you have two two...
cues.zh: 你还可以做多主，也就是有两个……

cues.en: You can have two Postgres databases that are writing to each other
cues.zh: 你可以让两个 Postgres 数据库互相写入

cues.en: and being kept up to sync that way.
cues.zh: 并通过这种方式保持同步。

cues.en: There's only one of these tools that supports that directly, is a tool called Buccardo.
cues.zh: 只有其中一个工具直接支持这一点，这个工具叫 Buccardo。

cues.en: So the bad part is these are a lot more complicated to set up than
cues.zh: 所以不好的一面是，这些工具的搭建比

cues.en: standard streaming replication.
cues.zh: 标准的流复制要复杂得多。

cues.en: And schema changes have to be pushed out manually.
cues.zh: 而且架构变更必须手动推送。

cues.en: These tools won't do this for you because there's no trigger that fires when you add or change a table.
cues.zh: 这些工具不会替你处理，因为新增或修改表时没有触发器会触发。

cues.en: They pose significantly more overhead on the primary than
cues.zh: 它们给主服务器带来的开销远高于

cues.en: streaming replication because all these triggers go in... Going crazy.
cues.zh: 流复制，因为这些触发器都会……简直要疯了。

cues.en: Now something that's coming in nine point four and nine point five is a framework called logical decoding,
cues.zh: 现在，9.4 和 9.5 版本将引入一个名为逻辑解码的框架，

cues.en: which a lot of... Where this potential for what trigger based replication does now is being built into the Postgres core,
cues.zh: 它有很多……触发器复制如今能做到的这些功能，正在被集成到 Postgres 核心中，

cues.en: except it doesn't use triggers. It's part of the Postgres core.
cues.zh: 只是它不使用触发器，而是 Postgres 核心的一部分。

cues.en: The bad part is it's kind of experimental.
cues.zh: 不好的一点是，它还有点实验性。

cues.en: If you want, you can look for bidirectional replication and unidirectional replication
cues.zh: 如果你愿意，可以在 Postgres 上查查双向复制和单向复制

cues.en: on Postgres,
cues.zh: 的相关内容，

cues.en: but they have significant limitations, and it's still kind of a new technology.
cues.zh: 但它们有不少限制，而且这项技术还比较新。

cues.en: But great things are going to be coming in this department, like in nine point six and later.
cues.zh: 不过这个领域很快会有很大进展，比如 9.6 及之后的版本。

cues.en: Okay.
cues.zh: 好。

cues.en: Next thing I wanna go is... Over is transactions,
cues.zh: 接下来我想讲……接下来是事务、

cues.en: multi version concurrency control, and vacuuming.
cues.zh: 多版本并发控制和清理。

cues.en: For people who administer Postgres databases,
cues.zh: 对于管理 Postgres 数据库的人来说，

cues.en: vacuum is kind of this permanent
cues.zh: vacuum 就像是生活中一件长期

cues.en: thing in your life that you have to worry about.
cues.zh: 需要操心的事。

cues.en: It's actually not as big a deal as it's often made out to be, but you do have to understand what it is, why Postgres needs to do vacuuming,
cues.zh: 其实它没大家说得那么严重，但你确实得明白它是什么、Postgres 为什么需要执行 vacuum，

cues.en: and
cues.zh: 以及

cues.en: how to manage it.
cues.zh: 怎么管理它。

cues.en: So first of all,
cues.zh: 首先，

cues.en: starting with... Let's go back to first principles,
cues.zh: 我们从头说起……回到最基本的原理，

cues.en: a transaction
cues.zh: 数据库里的

cues.en: in a database.
cues.zh: 事务。

cues.en: A transaction is a unit of
cues.zh: 事务是一个

cues.en: which which... A unit of work which
cues.zh: 呃……一个工作单元，

cues.en: must be atomically applied to the database
cues.zh: 必须以原子方式应用到数据库中，

cues.en: and is invisible to every other database client until it's committed.
cues.zh: 而且在提交之前，其他数据库客户端都看不到它。

cues.en: So the classic example, no bank in the world actually works this way, but every example uses this, which is you have a transactions table with account ID and a value
cues.zh: 经典例子是这样的——现实中没哪家银行真这么运作，但所有示例都用它：你有一张交易表，包含账户 ID 和一个金额

cues.en: and and the offset account, and you add a $120 from this account and subtract a $120 from the matching account.
cues.zh: 以及对方账户，你从这个账户加 120 美元，再从对应账户减 120 美元。

cues.en: And you don't want a crash right here to have this recorded but not have that recorded. Either the whole thing gets recorded or none of it does.
cues.zh: 你不希望在这中间崩溃，导致这边记了账而那边没记。要么整个都记上，要么全都不记。

cues.en: Pretty simple.
cues.zh: 挺简单的。

cues.en: So once the commit completes,
cues.zh: 所以，提交完成之后，

cues.en: transact... Data's been written to permanent storage
cues.zh: 事务……数据就已经写入持久存储了，

cues.en: minus synchronous commit.
cues.zh: 同步提交除外。

cues.en: And if the... If the database... If a crash occurs, any transaction will be either committed or not. You will never see a half done transaction.
cues.zh: 如果……如果数据库……如果发生崩溃，事务要么已经提交，要么没有提交。你绝不会看到只完成一半的事务。

cues.en: And no transaction can directly see another transaction in progress,
cues.zh: 而且，一个事务无法直接看到另一个正在进行中的事务，

cues.en: so we'll never see just that first insert.
cues.zh: 所以我们绝不会只看到第一条插入记录。

cues.en: In PostgresQL, everything runs inside a transaction.
cues.zh: 在 PostgreSQL 中，所有操作都在事务中执行。

cues.en: So even if you just type a single statement, there's an implicit begin and end around those... Begin and commit around that single statement.
cues.zh: 所以哪怕你只输入一条语句，它也会被隐式地包裹在 begin 和 commit 之间。

cues.en: What this means is if you...
cues.zh: 这意味着如果你……

cues.en: Postgres has a very extensive set of programming
cues.zh: Postgres 提供了非常丰富的编程

cues.en: language facilities to let you write your own functions. And if those functions modify the database, they're running inside a transaction.
cues.zh: 语言特性，让你可以编写自定义函数。如果这些函数修改了数据库，它们也是在事务中运行的。

cues.en: So... And one of the nice parts about this is everything that modifies the database is transactional, even schema changes.
cues.zh: 所以……这里面很棒的一点是，所有修改数据库的操作都支持事务，甚至包括模式变更（schema changes）。

cues.en: You can type again, drop a table, type rollback, and that... And and the table's back again,
cues.zh: 你可以再输入命令，删掉一张表，再输入 rollback，然后……表又回来了，

cues.en: which is pretty nice.
cues.zh: 这还挺不错的。

cues.en: It means it makes doing database migrations a lot safer because you can wrap the whole migration inside a begin and an end.
cues.zh: 这让数据库迁移安全得多，因为你可以把整个迁移过程包在 begin 和 end 之间。

cues.en: And that way, if the the migration fails halfway through, it'll abort, and you won't have a half done migration. That's really nice.
cues.zh: 这样一来，如果迁移到一半失败了，就会中止，你也不会留下一个没完成的迁移。这很不错。

cues.en: One thing to note about transactions is there's a lot of resources that are held while a transaction is open, like temporary tables, like working memory, locks, especially locks.
cues.zh: 有一点要注意：事务打开期间会占用很多资源，比如临时表、工作内存和锁，尤其是锁。

cues.en: So keep transactions brief and to the point. Don't implement user visible features using transactions, like don't have a user cancel button be based on a transaction.
cues.zh: 所以事务要简短、直接。不要用事务实现用户可见的功能，比如不要让用户取消按钮依赖事务。

cues.en: That's not very common anymore because of web... Because web frameworks don't really support it, but it used to be a a thing.
cues.zh: 现在这种做法已经不太常见了，因为 Web……因为 Web 框架不太支持，不过过去确实有过这种做法。

cues.en: Don't have don't be... Don't have processes that are doing external
cues.zh: 不要让……不要让进程在事务中执行外部

cues.en: operations
cues.zh: 操作

cues.en: with a transaction like sending mail or scraping a web page or something like that, keep transactions short
cues.zh: 比如发送邮件、抓取网页之类的操作。要让事务保持简短

cues.en: because holding these resources is a big source of concurrency problems in Postgres.
cues.zh: 因为占用这些资源是 Postgres 并发问题的一大来源。

cues.en: Specifically,
cues.zh: 具体来说，

cues.en: aware of sessions in idle and transaction. We'll talk about this later when we talk about viewing what's going on in the database.
cues.zh: 要注意处于空闲和事务中的会话。稍后我们在讨论查看数据库运行状态时会再讲到这点。

cues.en: Django used to be notorious for creating lots and lots of idle and transaction sessions.
cues.zh: Django 过去因产生大量处于事务中的空闲会话而臭名昭著。

cues.en: It's now
cues.zh: 现在

cues.en: largely been fixed in the 09/06 and later...
cues.zh: 在 09/06 及之后的版本中很大程度上已经修复了……

cues.en: Or the 01/06, excuse me, later time frame.
cues.zh: 抱歉，更正一下，应该是在 01/06 之后的版本。

cues.en: Okay. Well, you know, we're all programmers. So, you know, if transactions would be easy if databases were single user, but thank goodness they're not.
cues.zh: 好的。大家都是程序员。所以你们懂的，如果数据库是单用户的，事务处理就会很简单，但谢天谢地它并不是单用户的。

cues.en: So how do we handle concurrency control
cues.zh: 那么，如何处理并发控制，

cues.en: when two sessions are trying to use the same data
cues.zh: 当两个会话试图使用同一份数据时，

cues.en: given what we need to do for transactions?
cues.zh: 同时还要满足事务的要求？

cues.en: So, you know, process one begins a transaction, and then process two begins a transaction, and then process one updates a tuple. Just a little terminology note.
cues.zh: 比如，进程一开始一个事务，然后进程二也开始一个事务，接着进程一更新一个元组。补充一点术语说明。

cues.en: Tuple and row mean the same thing.
cues.zh: 元组和行的意思相同。

cues.en: Tuple is kind of a database... Is a little bit more of a data... Database theory term,
cues.zh: 元组算是数据库……更偏向于数据……数据库理论中的术语，

cues.en: and row is more of a database engineer term.
cues.zh: 而行则更像是数据库工程师常用的说法。

cues.en: They mean exactly the same thing. Similarly, you'll hear me talk about columns
cues.zh: 它们指的完全是同一个东西。同样，你们也会听到我提到列、

cues.en: columns,
cues.zh: 列、

cues.en: fields, and attributes.
cues.zh: 字段和属性。

cues.en: Those all mean the same thing. And a table and a relation are the same thing.
cues.zh: 这些说的都是同一回事。而表和关系也是同一个概念。

cues.en: I tend to use the more...
cues.zh: 我更倾向于使用更……

cues.en: The Postgres tends to favor tuple
cues.zh: Postgres 更倾向于使用元组、

cues.en: attribute
cues.zh: 属性

cues.en: and relation, and I tend to use those terms. They just mean the same thing as row, column, and table, respectively.
cues.zh: 以及关系，我也习惯用这些术语。它们其实就分别对应行、列和表。

cues.en: And then process two tries to read the same tuple.
cues.zh: 然后进程 2 尝试读取同一个元组。

cues.en: So what do we do? How do we actually write the code that makes this work?
cues.zh: 那我们该怎么做？具体要怎么写代码来实现呢？

cues.en: So the problem is process two can't get the version
cues.zh: 所以问题是，进程二拿不到这个版本

cues.en: of the tuple that process one wrote
cues.zh: 进程一所写的那个元组

cues.en: because that transaction hasn't committed yet.
cues.zh: 因为那个事务还没有提交。

cues.en: So it needs to get that old version of the tuple, but where does it get it from?
cues.zh: 所以它需要拿到那个旧版本的元组，但它从哪里拿到呢？

cues.en: You know, does it does it... Do we keep it in memory... Around in memory?
cues.zh: 你知道，它会不会……我们要不要把它保留在内存里……一直放在内存里？

cues.en: On disk? Do we have a special rollback area? The old Oracle rollback buffer solution?
cues.zh: 在磁盘上？我们有没有专门的回滚区域？就是以前 Oracle 的回滚缓冲区方案？

cues.en: How do we actually write this code?
cues.zh: 这段代码到底该怎么写？

cues.en: And how do we make this code work if process one didn't touch one row but touched a quarter of a billion rows?
cues.zh: 如果进程一没碰一行，却碰了两亿五千万行，我们怎么让这段代码正常工作？

cues.en: We have to keep that quarter of a billion rows around somewhere so that transaction...
cues.zh: 我们得把那两亿五千万行留在某个地方，这样事务……

cues.en: So other transactions can still use them.
cues.zh: 这样其他事务还能继续使用它们。

cues.en: This is an interesting problem, and people fought with this problem for a long time.
cues.zh: 这是个有趣的问题，人们为此纠结了很久。

cues.en: The first approach was, let's lock the whole database,
cues.zh: 第一种思路是，干脆锁住整个数据库，

cues.en: single user database. This is MongoDB solution.
cues.zh: 单用户数据库。这就是 MongoDB 的方案。

cues.en: That proved suboptimal.
cues.zh: 事实证明，效果不太理想。

cues.en: Then they said, okay, that was a bad idea. We'll just lock the table. So if anyone writes the table, we'll just lock that table
cues.zh: 然后他们说，好吧，那是个糟糕的主意。我们干脆锁表吧。所以如果有人写入这张表，我们就直接锁住它

cues.en: against any other access until the commit happens.
cues.zh: 不允许其他任何访问，直到提交发生。

cues.en: That was
cues.zh: 那

cues.en: not the improvement they were hoping for.
cues.zh: 并不是他们期望的改进。

cues.en: We could just lock that particular tuple
cues.zh: 我们可以只锁那个特定的元组

cues.en: and say, Okay,
cues.zh: 并说，好吧，

cues.en: if process
cues.zh: 如果进程

cues.en: one writes the tuple and process two tries to read it, process two will just stop
cues.zh: 一写入该元组，而进程二尝试读取它，进程二就会停下来

cues.en: and wait for the commit, and then it gets the new version.
cues.zh: 等待提交，然后拿到新版本。

cues.en: Which works. That's a completely valid solution, but still not great from a concurrency point of view.
cues.zh: 这样确实能用。这是个完全有效的方案，但从并发的角度来看还是不太理想。

cues.en: Oracle's original solution is, Okay, we'll have this special rollback buffer. And we'll have code that says, oh, that tuple's been modified.
cues.zh: Oracle 最初的方案是：我们加一个特殊的回滚缓冲区，再写一些代码来标记：“哦，这个元组被修改了。”

cues.en: Let's go find the old version, and we'll pick it up out of this rollback area,
cues.zh: 我们去找旧版本，然后从这个回滚区里把它取出来，

cues.en: which
cues.zh: 这个方案

cues.en: was... Which also had
cues.zh: 还有……它也有

cues.en: significant performance
cues.zh: 显著的性能

cues.en: issues because every time it had... It had to keep rebuilding these old states for other processes.
cues.zh: 问题，因为每次……它都得为其他进程不断重建这些旧状态。

cues.en: So none of those were really satisfactory.
cues.zh: 所以这些都不太令人满意。

cues.en: Postgres was the first kind of major database
cues.zh: Postgres 是第一个

cues.en: to use multi version concurrency control,
cues.zh: 采用多版本并发控制的主流数据库，

cues.en: which is Postgres' solution.
cues.zh: 这就是 Postgres 的解决方案。

cues.en: Postgres' solution is we'll keep both
cues.zh: Postgres 的方案是，我们把两个

cues.en: tuples around,
cues.zh: 元组都保留下来，

cues.en: Both the old and the new version or process... Better put, process one's version and process two's version
cues.zh: 旧版本和新版本，或者说……更准确地说，进程一的版本和进程二的版本

cues.en: will still... Will exist on disk as first class tuples right next to each other.
cues.zh: 仍然会……会作为一等元组一起存在于磁盘上，彼此相邻。

cues.en: And so... And we'll mark them as to which transactions can see
cues.zh: 然后……然后我们会标记它们，说明哪些事务能看到

cues.en: those versions.
cues.zh: 这些版本。

cues.en: And the collection of things a particular transaction can see is called a snapshot in Postgres.
cues.zh: 在 Postgres 中，某个特定事务能看到的所有数据的集合，被称为快照（snapshot）。

cues.en: And these are actually first class members of the database. You can manipulate them if you want. It's kinda crazy.
cues.zh: 而且它们在数据库里其实是一等公民，你甚至可以直接操作它们，简直不可思议。

cues.en: One of the things to remember is there's no real snapshot.
cues.zh: 但有一点要记住：并不存在真正物理意义上的快照。

cues.en: Process one's view of the database and process two's view of the database are both perfectly equally valid views of the database. They're just different because one's made changes the other can't see.
cues.zh: 进程一看到的数据库视角，和进程二看到的，完全具有同等的有效性；它们只是有所不同，因为其中一个做了修改，而另一个还看不到。

cues.en: So this has... This... Now now lots of databases use this. Even SQLite has an MVCC implementation
cues.zh: 现在很多数据库都在使用它。甚至 SQLite 也有一个 MVCC 的实现，

cues.en: because it works really, really well.
cues.zh: 因为它的效果真的非常好。

cues.en: Readers don't block readers.
cues.zh: 读操作不会阻塞读操作。

cues.en: Readers don't block writers.
cues.zh: 读操作不会阻塞写操作。

cues.en: So
cues.zh: 所以，

cues.en: writers don't block readers because
cues.zh: 写操作也不会阻塞读操作，因为

cues.en: you can modify the tuple and just pick
cues.zh: 你可以修改元组，并且直接读取

cues.en: it up and you
cues.zh: 它，你

cues.en: can read a tuple that someone else has modified.
cues.zh: 也可以读取别人已经修改过的元组。

cues.en: The only time we have to block is if two processes try to write to the same tuple,
cues.zh: 唯一需要阻塞的情况，是两个进程试图写入同一个元组，

cues.en: because then the database would kind of fork.
cues.zh: 因为那样的话，数据库就有点像分叉了。

cues.en: There could be two different versions of the database forever, and we don't allow that because we need to resolve them somehow into a single version and,
cues.zh: 数据库可能永远存在两个不同的版本，但我们不允许这样，因为我们得想办法把它们合并成一个版本，然后，

cues.en: you know, brains start to hurt.
cues.zh: 你知道，脑子都快疼了。

cues.en: So each transaction maintains its own snapshot of the database.
cues.zh: 所以每个事务都会维护自己的数据库快照。

cues.en: In a... You can almost think of it as when you type begin, Postgres cop makes a copy of the database for you.
cues.zh: 可以……你几乎可以这么理解：当你输入 begin 时，Postgres cop 会为你复制一份数据库。

cues.en: It doesn't really work that way, of course, because that would be kind of nuts.
cues.zh: 当然，实际并不是这么运作的，那样也太离谱了。

cues.en: But you can think of it that you are working in your own little copy of the database.
cues.zh: 你可以把它想成：你在自己的数据库副本里操作。

cues.en: When it makes that... It can make that copy one of two times, either when you type... You say begin. And then in that case, inside the entire transaction,
cues.zh: 它可以在两个时机之一创建这个副本：要么在你输入……说“开始”时。这样，在整个事务期间，

cues.en: even if other parts of... Even if other processes are changing the database,
cues.zh: 即使其他部分……即使其他进程正在修改数据库，

cues.en: you only see your changes.
cues.zh: 你也只能看到自己的修改。

cues.en: Or it can create the snapshot every every time you type a statement.
cues.zh: 或者，它可以在你每次输入一条语句时创建快照。

cues.en: And that way, if some other processes are committing,
cues.zh: 这样一来，如果有其他进程正在提交，

cues.en: even though you're inside one transaction, you still see the changes. Does that distinction make sense to people?
cues.zh: 即便你处在同一个事务中，也依然能看到这些变更。大家能理解这个区别吗？

cues.en: You're inside your own transaction.
cues.zh: 你在你自己的事务中。

cues.en: You you have two possibilities. One is you're completely isolated.
cues.zh: 你有两种可能。一种是你被完全隔离了。

cues.en: You never see any other changes until until you commit.
cues.zh: 直到你提交之前，你都看不到任何其他变更。

cues.en: Or
cues.zh: 或者，

cues.en: every... You see other people's commits, but they can't see yours because you haven't committed yet.
cues.zh: 每……你能看到其他人的提交，但他们看不到你的，因为你还没有提交。

cues.en: So you can think of those as two different modes of operation.
cues.zh: 所以你可以把它们看作两种不同的运行模式。

cues.en: And in fact, that's what they're called, transaction isolation modes.
cues.zh: 事实上，它们就被称为事务隔离模式。

cues.en: And
cues.zh: 而且

cues.en: the problem is MVCC does have some limitations.
cues.zh: 问题在于 MVCC 确实有一些局限性。

cues.en: You you can't fork the database
cues.zh: 你没法把数据库给分叉

cues.en: as in two different processes change the same tuple in two
cues.zh: 比如两个不同的进程改了同一个元组，以两种

cues.en: different change the same tuple.
cues.zh: 不同的……改了同一个元组。

cues.en: I was about to say change the same tuple in incompatible ways, but Postgres doesn't
cues.zh: 我刚才差点说成“以不兼容的方式修改同一元组”，但 Postgres 其实根本不会

cues.en: check to see if you wrote the same data. It just if any
cues.zh: 去检查你写的是否是相同的数据。它只是只要有任何

cues.en: two different processes try and change the same tuple,
cues.zh: 两个不同的进程试图去修改同一个元组，

cues.en: Postgres won't let that happen.
cues.zh: Postgres 就绝不允许这种情况发生。

cues.en: So it will... And it will it will prevent it either with locking,
cues.zh: 这样一来……它会通过锁来防止冲突：

cues.en: where if you try to change a tuple someone else has, you'll wait until they commit, and then you can make your change. Or it'll throw an error by saying,
cues.zh: 如果你想修改别人持有的元组，就得等对方提交，然后你才能修改。或者，它会报错说：

cues.en: you're touching a tuple someone else is, and I'm not gonna let you do that. Yes?
cues.zh: 你正在操作别人正在操作的元组，我不会让你这么做。对吧？

cues.en: Then it's up to the master master tool to figure out how to make that work.
cues.zh: 然后就由主控工具来想办法处理。

cues.en: Yeah. Usually, it's last one wins is is what happens there. But that's a little bit outside MVCC.
cues.zh: 对。通常的情况是最后一次修改生效。不过这有点超出 MVCC 的范畴了。

cues.en: You know, that's... So that's the next level up above MVCC.
cues.zh: 你看，这就是……这比 MVCC 又高了一个层级。

cues.en: So
cues.zh: 所以

cues.en: you can have conflicts in this because
cues.zh: 这里可能会发生冲突，因为

cues.en: if two different processes try and change the same tuple,
cues.zh: 如果两个不同的进程试图修改同一个元组，

cues.en: then you have to resolve that conflict somehow. And Postgres either does it with locking where one one just takes a number and weights
cues.zh: 那你就得想办法解决冲突。Postgres 会通过锁来处理，一个进程先拿到一个编号，然后排在

cues.en: behind the one... The first one that changed the tuple. And then when that process commits, it gets to make its change.
cues.zh: 第一个修改元组的进程后面……等那个进程提交之后，它才能完成自己的修改。

cues.en: Or
cues.zh: 或者

cues.en: it takes a number of weights, if that other process commits,
cues.zh: 它需要一系列权重，如果另一个进程提交了，

cues.en: you get an error saying, you know, I was trying to give you a perfect model of the database, but I can't anymore because the database has changed in an incompatible way.
cues.zh: 你就会收到一个错误提示，大意是：我本想给你一个数据库的完美模型，但现在做不到了，因为数据库已经以不兼容的方式发生了变化。

cues.en: And which one it does is based on this thing called an isolation mode.
cues.zh: 至于具体采用哪种方式，取决于所谓的隔离模式。

cues.en: The default is called recommitted.
cues.zh: 默认的叫做读已提交（read committed）。

cues.en: There's also repeatable read and serializable.
cues.zh: 此外还有可重复读（repeatable read）和可串行化（serializable）。

cues.en: The SQL standard also gives you read uncommitted. Postgres doesn't support that. And MySQL claims it supports it, but it lies because it doesn't actually do it right.
cues.zh: SQL 标准还提供了读未提交（read uncommitted）。Postgres 不支持它。而 MySQL 声称支持，但它在撒谎，因为它实际上并没有正确实现。

cues.en: So in recommitted,
cues.zh: 所以在 recommitted 模式下，

cues.en: each statement starts its own snapshot. And that means it sees anything that's committed since the last statement. So while you're inside your transaction and recommitted,
cues.zh: 每条语句都会开启自己的快照。这意味着它能看到自上一条语句以来提交的所有内容。所以当你处于事务中，并使用 recommitted 模式时，

cues.en: you... The database could be changing.
cues.zh: 你……数据库可能正在发生变化。

cues.en: Your view of the database could be changing because other processes are committing and writing data to the database and things are happening. And that's usually fine. That's not weird.
cues.zh: 你看到的数据库状态也可能在变化，因为其他进程正在提交事务、向数据库写入数据，事情还在不断发生。这通常没什么问题，也不奇怪。

cues.en: It just means you're not completely in your own isolated copy of the database.
cues.zh: 这只是说，你并没有完全在自己独立的数据库副本里操作。

cues.en: In this case, if you try and change a tuple that another transaction is touched, it blocks until that... You you block until that transaction commits.
cues.zh: 在这种情况下，如果你尝试修改另一个事务碰过的元组，操作就会被阻塞，直到……你会一直等到那个事务提交。

cues.en: But you might say, Well, okay, that sounds... I need something stronger than that. I want to be able to run-in my own private copy of the database so that even if the database... Other processes change the database,
cues.zh: 但你可能会说：“好吧，听起来……我需要比这更强的保证。我希望能在自己的私有数据库副本里运行，这样即使数据库……其他进程修改了数据库，

cues.en: I still see what happened when I issued begin.
cues.zh: 我仍然能看到执行 begin 时数据库的状态。

cues.en: That mode exists. That's called repeatable read.
cues.zh: 这种模式确实存在。叫做可重复读。

cues.en: That way, if you do two selects in a row, you're for sure going to get the same result.
cues.zh: 这样，如果你连续做两次select，就一定能得到相同的结果。

cues.en: In repeatable read, you might get different results depending on what... Who else is committed while you were doing the the first select.
cues.zh: 在可重复读模式下，你可能会得到不同的结果，这取决于……在你执行第一次select期间，还有谁提交了事务。

cues.en: Does that make sense? Okay.
cues.zh: 这样讲能理解吗？好。

cues.en: And the snapshot lasts until the commit.
cues.zh: 这个快照会一直持续到提交。

cues.en: If you modify... If you try to modify a tuple that another transaction has already changed,
cues.zh: 如果你修改……如果你试图修改一个已经被另一个事务修改过的元组，

cues.en: you block,
cues.zh: 你就会被阻塞，

cues.en: and then you get an error
cues.zh: 然后你会收到一个错误，

cues.en: instead of just in... If that other transaction commits.
cues.zh: 而不是……如果那个其他事务已提交的话。

cues.en: Because Postgres has thrown up its hands and said, You know,
cues.zh: 因为 Postgres 已经放弃了，它说：“你知道吗，

cues.en: you asked for a perfectly clean copy of the database, but I can't give you that anymore.
cues.zh: 你要的是一份完全干净的数据库副本，但我现在已经没法给你了。”

cues.en: So now here... So you get an error instead.
cues.zh: 所以现在……你拿到的会是一个错误。

cues.en: And that's called a serialization failure.
cues.zh: 这就叫序列化失败。

cues.en: So it tries to maintain the illusion of a perfect snapshot, but if it can't, it throws an error.
cues.zh: 它会尽力维持完美快照的假象，但要是做不到，就会报错。

cues.en: What usually happens then is the application then just retries the transaction. It says, oh, that didn't work. Back around it goes.
cues.zh: 通常这时候，应用会重试这笔事务。它会说：“哦，刚才没成功。”然后再来一次。

cues.en: There is a higher... There's an even higher level of isolation called serializable
cues.zh: 还有一个更高的隔离级别……叫可串行化。

cues.en: because not every conflict can be resolved at the protuple level. For example, suppose you have a... You you do a count
cues.zh: 因为并非所有冲突都能在原型层面解决。比如，假设你有一个……你你做一次计数

cues.en: on a table and say, if that count comes back as zero, insert a row.
cues.zh: 放在桌上，然后说，如果那个计数返回为零，就插入一行。

cues.en: Even in serializable mode,
cues.zh: 即使在可串行化模式下，

cues.en: even even in repeatable read mode, you could get the wrong result because someone else could insert the... You could do the count, get back zero, go back to your application. Meantime, someone else counts,
cues.zh: 哪怕在可重复读模式下，你也可能得到错误的结果，因为其他人可能会插入……你查了数量，返回是零，然后回到你的应用。在此期间，其他人也进行了统计，

cues.en: gets
cues.zh: 获取

cues.en: back zero, and inserts the row. You come back and insert the row, and now there are two rows where there really should have only been one.
cues.zh: 返回 0 并插入了该行。接着你又回来插入了该行，结果原本应该只有一行的地方，现在却有了两行。

cues.en: You know, inserting calculated values is the typical case here. Serializable actually will detect those cases
cues.zh: 你知道，这里通常会插入计算出来的值。Serializable 实际上会检测到这些情况

cues.en: and throw a serialization error.
cues.zh: 然后抛出序列化错误。

cues.en: It requires some extra overhead. There's a... It uses a mechanism called predicate locking. Basically, it keeps track of what queries have been done and will throw a serialization failure if you do something that invalidates the result of a previous query.
cues.zh: 这会带来一些额外开销。它使用一种叫作谓词锁的机制。简单来说，它会跟踪执行过哪些查询；如果某个操作会导致之前查询的结果失效，就会抛出序列化失败错误。

cues.en: But it's actually quite efficient. Postgres is the only database that has this, by the way.
cues.zh: 不过它其实相当高效。顺便说一下，Postgres 是唯一支持这一机制的数据库。

cues.en: I often,
cues.zh: 我经常

cues.en: for new applications, suggest that while you're developing it, you run-in serializable mode because you may be surprised
cues.zh: 建议开发新应用时，先以可串行化模式运行。你可能会惊讶于

cues.en: at what
cues.zh: 自己对

cues.en: assumptions you make about the access patterns in your database.
cues.zh: 数据库访问模式做了哪些假设。

cues.en: Anyway, so
cues.zh: 总之，

cues.en: there's some consequences to MVCC.
cues.zh: MVCC 会带来一些影响。

cues.en: So the biggest
cues.zh: 其中最重要的

cues.en: consequence that you need to be aware of is if you go and delete a bunch of tuples and then commit,
cues.zh: 一点是：如果你删除了一堆元组然后提交，

cues.en: those are not automatically returned to free space.
cues.zh: 这些空间不会自动回到空闲空间中。

cues.en: The reason is other transactions may still be able to see them.
cues.zh: 原因是其他事务可能仍然能看到这些行。

cues.en: That
cues.zh: 这样

cues.en: makes sense.
cues.zh: 就说得通了。

cues.en: You you can imagine two transactions running in parallel.
cues.zh: 你可以想象有两个事务并行运行。

cues.en: One of them deletes a ton of rows, and then the second one, which is running in repeatable read mode,
cues.zh: 其中一个删除了大量行，而第二个事务以可重复读模式运行，

cues.en: does a query that would that would... That needs to access those.
cues.zh: 它执行了一个需要访问这些行的查询……

cues.en: So we still... We can't clean them up yet. We can't release them to free space because they're still valid rows as far as the second transaction is concerned.
cues.zh: 所以我们还不能清理它们，也不能释放它们占用的空间，因为在第二个事务看来，这些行仍然有效。

cues.en: The result is that there needs... That
cues.zh: 结果就是，我们可能需要……也就是说

cues.en: we may not be able to readily check on every commit if we can return things to free space or not,
cues.zh: 我们可能没法在每次提交时都及时检查，能不能把空间释放出来，

cues.en: which means that that ultimately
cues.zh: 这就意味着，归根结底，

cues.en: these tuples are in fact dead. No transaction could ever see them, but we haven't freed them yet.
cues.zh: 这些元组确实已经失效了。没有任何事务能再看到它们，但我们还没有释放它们。

cues.en: So we need a process that goes through and cleans those dead tuples up, and that's what vacuum does.
cues.zh: 所以我们需要一个进程来清理这些失效的元组，这就是 vacuum 的作用。

cues.en: The... So when you hear people talk about Postgres vacuum, that's its primary function,
cues.zh: 所以……当你听人们谈起 Postgres 的 vacuum 时，它的主要作用就是

cues.en: is to go through each table, find dead tuples that no transaction can ever see again, and release them back into free space so they can be re... Reused.
cues.zh: 遍历每张表，找出任何事务都再也看不到的失效元组，并将它们释放回空闲空间，以便……重新利用。

cues.en: So far so good?
cues.zh: 到这儿还好吧？

cues.en: So this is its primary job. It does other stuff, but this is the main thing it does.
cues.zh: 所以这是它的主要工作。它还会干别的，但这是它干的主要事情。

cues.en: Now the good news is,
cues.zh: 好消息是，

cues.en: generally, you don't have to do anything.
cues.zh: 一般来说，你什么都不用做。

cues.en: Postgres has a subsystem called auto vacuum that runs in the background that does this for you. Most small Postgres installations,
cues.zh: Postgres 有个叫 auto vacuum 的子系统在后台运行，帮你做这件事。大多数小型 Postgres 安装，

cues.en: small being defined as tens of gigabytes,
cues.zh: 小指的是几十 GB 的规模，

cues.en: never even
cues.zh: 根本

cues.en: know vacuuming exists.
cues.zh: 不知道 vacuum 的存在。

cues.en: It just happens. It's magic.
cues.zh: 它就那么自动发生了。很神奇。

cues.en: And that's... And
cues.zh: 而且……而且

cues.en: the... Its standard tuning is fine for most Postgres installations.
cues.zh: 它……它的标准配置对大多数 Postgres 安装来说就够用了。

cues.en: The other thing vacuum does while it's running is a step called analyze.
cues.zh: vacuum 在运行过程中还会做另一件事，就是执行一个叫 analyze 的步骤。

cues.en: Because the plan... The query planner needs statistics
cues.zh: 因为查询计划……查询规划器需要统计信息

cues.en: to decide how much... To decide
cues.zh: 来决定多少……来决定

cues.en: to generate good queries. For example, how many table... How many rows are in a table,
cues.zh: 生成好的查询。比如，表里有多少……表里有多少行，

cues.en: how the the values are distributed within a table.
cues.zh: 表内的值是如何分布的。

cues.en: And the analyzer...
cues.zh: 而分析器……

cues.en: And analyze picks up this information and records it in the database.
cues.zh: analyze 会收集这些信息并记录到数据库中。

cues.en: This happens...
cues.zh: 这发生在……

cues.en: Vacuum doesn't... Generally doesn't analyze too.
cues.zh: vacuum 通常不会……不会同时执行 analyze。

cues.en: However,
cues.zh: 不过，

cues.en: it is a background process. So if you do a major database change, like you restore from a p g restore,
cues.zh: 它是一个后台进程。所以如果你对数据库做了重大改动，比如用 pg_restore 恢复数据库，

cues.en: p g dump style backup,
cues.zh: 恢复自 pg_dump 格式的备份，

cues.en: you need to do an analyze to rebuild these statistics. Similarly, if you do a bulk insert,
cues.zh: 你就需要运行 analyze 来重建这些统计信息。同样，如果你批量插入数据，

cues.en: it may take a while for the analyze step to catch up and and the auto vacuum daemon to come along and analyze that table. So it's a good idea to do a manual analyze.
cues.zh: analyze 步骤可能要过一会儿才能完成，自动清理守护进程也需要时间才会来分析这张表。所以手动运行 analyze 是个好主意。

cues.en: And it's just an analyze command, analyze semicolon return.
cues.zh: 只要运行 analyze 命令，输入 analyze 再按回车就行。

cues.en: Sometimes you'll hear somebody complain, vacuum's not working, often because the table is getting big.
cues.zh: 有时你会听到有人抱怨：真空机制没起作用，通常是因为表越来越大。

cues.en: Vacuum is probably working.
cues.zh: Vacuum 可能正在运行。

cues.en: It is rare that vacuum
cues.zh: 真空状态很少见。

cues.en: is the source of the problem.
cues.zh: 是问题的根源。

cues.en: Part of it is
cues.zh: 其中一部分原因是

cues.en: Postgres databases tend to be on disk somewhat larger than those on other database systems like Oracle.
cues.zh: Postgres 数据库在磁盘上往往比其他数据库系统（比如 Oracle）的更大一些。

cues.en: They tend to stabilize between
cues.zh: 它们往往会稳定在某个范围。

cues.en: bloat,
cues.zh: 臃肿，

cues.en: which is to say
cues.zh: 也就是说

cues.en: space
cues.zh: 空间

cues.en: that is not
cues.zh: 那不是

cues.en: being used for live data but is still allocated on disk, that's acceptable in a Postgres database. So if you just see a table start out at
cues.zh: 用于实时数据，但仍然分配在磁盘上，这在 Postgres 数据库里是可以接受的。所以，如果你看到一张表一开始大小是

cues.en: five gigabytes and ends up at about 7.5 gigabytes,
cues.zh: 从 5 GB 一路涨到大约 7.5 GB，

cues.en: that's fine.
cues.zh: 没问题。

cues.en: Sometimes people will look and see these auto vacuum daemon workers running in panic and say, what what... What's going on? Why why are these things running? Sometimes they're running for a long time on large tables. That's Okay.
cues.zh: 有时，人们看到这些自动清理守护进程的工作线程惊慌地运行，就会问：“这这……是怎么回事？为什么为什么它们在运行？”有时，它们会在大表上运行很长时间。这没问题。

cues.en: They're doing their job.
cues.zh: 它们只是在做自己的工作。

cues.en: Say, no, really, vacuum's not working. For example, a table is starting to expand much faster than you would expect given the insert and delete rates.
cues.zh: 有人会说：“不，真的，清理机制没起作用。”比如，一张表开始膨胀，速度远超插入和删除速率所能解释的程度。

cues.en: The first thing to look at are their long running transactions
cues.zh: 首先要关注的是那些长期运行的事务

cues.en: open.
cues.zh: 打开着。

cues.en: Transactions can block auto vacuum because
cues.zh: 事务可能会阻塞自动清理，因为

cues.en: as far as auto vacuum is concerned, those tuples are still visible because there's this long running transaction.
cues.zh: 在自动清理看来，那些元组仍然可见，因为有一个长期运行的事务。

cues.en: Look for sessions marked idle in transaction, and we'll show later how to do that.
cues.zh: 找出标记为“事务中空闲”的会话，稍后我们会演示怎么做。

cues.en: Because an idle in transaction session means that there is an open transaction that's just sitting there,
cues.zh: 因为“事务中空闲”表示有一个打开的事务就这么闲置着，

cues.en: and that can block vacuuming.
cues.zh: 这会阻碍清理。

cues.en: Are you doing manual table locking, issuing actual lock statements against the database?
cues.zh: 你是在手动锁表吗？会直接对数据库执行锁定语句吗？

cues.en: You shouldn't be. Generally, there's almost always a way of designing your day... Your application so you don't need to do that. But
cues.zh: 你不该这么做。一般来说，几乎总有办法设计你的应用，让你不必这么做。不过

cues.en: exclusive locks on the database that you take manually can block vacuuming.
cues.zh: 你手动加在数据库上的排他锁可能会阻塞清理操作。

cues.en: Very high write rate tables
cues.zh: 写入频率非常高的表

cues.en: can...
cues.zh: 可能会……

cues.en: You're doing zillions of updates to a table, and that generates a lot of dead tuples.
cues.zh: 你对一张表执行了海量更新，这会产生很多死元组。

cues.en: Because an update in Postgres is basically a delete plus an insert.
cues.zh: 因为在 Postgres 中，更新操作本质上就是一次删除加一次插入。

cues.en: It may be that autovacuum isn't able to keep up with the level of
cues.zh: 这可能是因为 autovacuum 跟不上

cues.en: traffic that you're giving to a particular table, in which case you may want to manually vacuum it.
cues.zh: 某个特定表所承受的流量级别，这种情况下你可能需要手动对它进行 vacuum。

cues.en: Or do you have lots of tables, like 10,000 plus tables? That seems crazy,
cues.zh: 或者你是不是有大量的表，比如超过 10,000 张表？这听起来很疯狂，

cues.en: but some applications do schema based sharding where they give each user or each client their own schema. And if that schema has a 100 user... A 100 tables, which is a perfectly reasonable number of tables, and there are a 100 clients on a single database, there's 10,000 tables right there.
cues.zh: 但有些应用会采用基于 schema 的分片，给每个用户或租户分配独立的 schema。如果每个 schema 有 100 个用……100 张表（这完全是个合理的数量），而单台数据库上有 100 个租户，那一下子就有了 10,000 张表。

cues.en: If you have... In that circumstance,
cues.zh: 如果你遇到这种情况……

cues.en: you have lots and lots and lots of tables, you generally want to increase the number of auto vacuum workers, which is by default three. Bump that up to 10 or 15 so that it can
cues.zh: 如果表特别多，通常就要增加自动清理工作进程的数量。默认是 3 个，可以调到 10 或 15 个，这样它才能

cues.en: keep up with the... Because each
cues.zh: 跟上……因为每次

cues.en: run only applies to a single table.
cues.zh: 运行只会处理一张表。

cues.en: The easiest thing to do is reduce the auto vacuum sleep time
cues.zh: 最简单的办法是缩短自动清理的休眠时间，

cues.en: or increase the number of auto vacuum workers, especially if you have lots of tables.
cues.zh: 或者增加自动清理工作进程的数量，尤其是表特别多的时候。

cues.en: Do manual vacuums at low periods
cues.zh: 在低峰时段手动执行 vacuum

cues.en: so that to
cues.zh: 这样一来

cues.en: keep up with it if you have...
cues.zh: 如果你们有……也能跟得上

cues.en: That way you're doing
cues.zh: 这样你就是在

cues.en: vacuuming at times when there's not a lot of traffic already.
cues.zh: 流量本来就不大的时候做 vacuum。

cues.en: And fix the broken stuff, idle in transaction sessions, long transactions, manual locking.
cues.zh: 还要修复坏掉的东西、事务中的空闲会话、长事务、手动加锁。

cues.en: The other thing you'll hear about is
cues.zh: 你还会听到的另一个说法是

cues.en: that
cues.zh: 就是

cues.en: that that auto vacuum is taking up too much time. And my serialized, it's never twins. It's never lupus, and it's never auto vacuum. You know? When people complain about load on the system, they almost always blame the auto vacuum daemon, and it's almost never the auto vacuum daemon.
cues.zh: 就是 autovacuum 占用了太多时间。而我的序列化，从来不是狼人。从来不是狼人，也从来不是 autovacuum。你知道吗？当人们抱怨系统负载时，几乎总是怪罪 autovacuum 守护进程，而几乎从来都不是 autovacuum 守护进程的问题。

cues.en: The easiest way to diagnose this is you can turn off autovacuum.
cues.zh: 排查这个问题最简单的方法，就是把 autovacuum 关掉。

cues.en: Set autovacuum equals off in postgresql.conf.
cues.zh: 在 postgresql.conf 里设置 autovacuum = off。

cues.en: Never do this permanently.
cues.zh: 千万别一直关着。

cues.en: Only do it temporarily.
cues.zh: 只能临时关一下。

cues.en: And then see if that reduces load on the system. The answer will probably be the system is still heavily loaded even with auto vacuum off. And then you know that wasn't the culprit. But never leave auto vacuum off
cues.zh: 然后看看系统负载有没有降下来。结果大概率是即使关了 autovacuum，系统负载依然很高。这样你就知道它不是罪魁祸首了。但千万别一直关着 autovacuum，

cues.en: because a database that's not being vacuumed will start bloating very badly.
cues.zh: 因为一个不做 vacuum 的数据库很快就会严重膨胀。

cues.en: If the problem really is auto vacuum,
cues.zh: 如果问题确实出在自动清理上，

cues.en: is to...
cues.zh: 就是……

cues.en: I say reduce here, is an unfortunate choice of terms. It's actually auto vacuum
cues.zh: 我这里说“减少”不太准确。实际上是自动清理

cues.en: auto vacuum vacuum cost delay.
cues.zh: 自动清理的清理成本延迟。

cues.en: That basically, if you... It's default twenty milliseconds,
cues.zh: 基本上，如果你……默认值是 20 毫秒，

cues.en: change by increasing delay to a hundred milliseconds. I'm not quite sure why I do that there. We'll call it reduce there. But this increases the amount of wait time
cues.zh: 把延迟调高到 100 毫秒。我不太确定我为什么要这么做。这里就叫它“减少”吧。不过，这会增加等待时间

cues.en: between cycles of the autovacuum daemon, and that will... That's usually enough to fix vacuum... Excessive vacuum load.
cues.zh: 也就是自动清理守护进程两轮运行之间的间隔。这样通常就足以解决清理负载过高的问题。

cues.en: So I'm not gonna go into the tedious details of vacuum freeze, which is a separate operation from vacuum. But what a vacuum freeze is is kind of a periodic major vacuum the PostgresQL has to do to prevent this really horrible thing that can happen called transaction ID wraparound.
cues.zh: 我就不细讲 vacuum freeze 繁琐的细节了，它是独立于 vacuum 的操作。但 vacuum freeze 本质上是 PostgreSQL 必须定期进行的一种深度清理，用来防止一种极其可怕的情况——事务 ID 回卷（wraparound）。

cues.en: It's generally not a problem,
cues.zh: 这通常不是什么大问题，

cues.en: but
cues.zh: 但是，

cues.en: and you'll see this occasionally in the law... In the in the...
cues.zh: 你偶尔也会在日志……在……在……

cues.en: When the autovacuum daemon is running because it'll say autovacuum to prevent XID wraparound.
cues.zh: 在 autovacuum 守护进程运行时看到它，因为日志会显示“autovacuum to prevent XID wraparound”。

cues.en: Generally, you don't have to worry about it, but for high IO load databases,
cues.zh: 一般来说，你不用担心这个问题，但对于 IO 负载很高的数据库，

cues.en: the IO can be an issue because it has to read and write entire tables. It has to read entire tables and potentially write them as well.
cues.zh: IO 可能会成为问题，因为它必须读写整张表。它得读取整张表，必要时还得写回去。

cues.en: One way you can handle... Solve this is to do a manual vacuum freeze at low, low periods. I did once... My standard recommendation for sites that are primarily based in The United States is to do a
cues.zh: 一种处理方法……解决办法是在负载较低的时候手动执行 VACUUM FREEZE。我曾经……对于主要面向美国用户的网站，我的标准建议是每

cues.en: man... To do a manual vacuum freeze on the fourth
cues.zh: 手动……在每月第四个

cues.en: on...
cues.zh: ……上手动执行 VACUUM FREEZE。

cues.en: To 3AM on Christmas Day and the July 4 because those tend to be really low low periods. I did present that to one client, and they gave me this look. And I realized I was talking to a client that ran emergency rooms.
cues.zh: 在圣诞节当天凌晨 3 点和 7 月 4 日，因为那段时间通常特别冷清。我把这个建议告诉过一位客户，他们看我的眼神让我意识到，我面对的是一家急诊室的运营方。

cues.en: It said 4AM on the July 4 and Christmas Day are not low, low periods for an emergency room. It's like... So adapt to your local conditions.
cues.zh: 他们说，7 月 4 日和圣诞节当天凌晨 4 点，急诊室可不冷清。就是这么回事……所以要根据当地情况调整。

cues.en: But generally, you want to run this, like, every one to four months, up to six months for a smaller site,
cues.zh: 不过一般来说，你要每隔一到四个月运行一次；规模较小的网站可以延长到六个月，

cues.en: And it depends on how many transactions you're doing.
cues.zh: 这取决于你处理的交易量。

cues.en: And you use the built in VacuumDB tool to do this, VacuumDB All Freeze Analyze.
cues.zh: 你可以用内置的 VacuumDB 工具来做这件事，VacuumDB All Freeze Analyze。

cues.en: And the idea here is you can't keep it from doing a vacuum freeze because if you
cues.zh: 这里的思路是，你没法阻止它执行 vacuum freeze，因为如果你

cues.en: keep try it too long from doing a vacuum freeze, it will ultimately shut your database down, and you probably don't want that.
cues.zh: 让它太久不执行 vacuum freeze，它最终会关掉你的数据库，而你大概不想那样。

cues.en: But you can move the IO to lower load periods.
cues.zh: 但你可以把 IO 挪到负载较低的时段。

cues.en: Okay. And there's vacuuming.
cues.zh: 好。还有 vacuum 操作。

cues.zh: 关于这个有问题吗？

cues.zh: 嗯，

cues.en: also for
cues.zh: 还有对它们做

cues.zh: vacuum 的话，

cues.zh: 我最后是这么做的：我们其实用 Python 写了个工具，它会定期醒来，vacuum 一张表，再睡去。醒来，vacuum 一张表，再睡去。你其实可以去看。如果你看 PG Experts 的 GitHub 仓库，有个叫 Flexible Freeze 的项目。
