cues.zh: 接下来聊 Schema 设计。其实我完全可以花上

cues.en: two of these things talking about all the schema design stuff. So I just want to go over some basic stuff that I see a lot.
cues.zh: 整整两场分享的篇幅去讲 Schema 设计。所以这里我只想过一遍我经常见到的基础内容。

cues.en: It's a deep topic, and this is just kind of random important things, especially for people who are not super familiar with Postgres.
cues.zh: 这是个很深的课题，我挑出来的只是一些重点零碎知识，尤其是针对不太熟悉 Postgres 的同学。

cues.en: So null.
cues.zh: 首先是 Null。

cues.en: Null is a total pain in the neck. There's no other way of getting around it. Every time you think you understand null, there's another exceptional case comes up where null does not behave the way you expect it to. People
cues.zh: Null 简直太让人头疼了，真的避无可避。每当你以为自己搞懂了 Null，就会冒出另一个例外情况，表现完全出乎你的意料。大家

cues.en: say that, well, SQL has a three value logic system, true, false, and null. And that's really generous because it implies there's some consistency behind the logic of null.
cues.zh: 总说，SQL 采用的是三值逻辑系统：True、False 和 Null。但这种说法实在太客气了，因为它暗示了 Null 背后的逻辑是有一致性的。

cues.en: You know, sometimes
cues.zh: 你知道，有时候

cues.en: you have to deal with null, but one of the things is only use it in your schema to mean missing value.
cues.zh: 你不得不处理 null，但有一点要记住：只在 Schema 中用它表示缺失值。

cues.en: Don't use it as a flag value.
cues.zh: 不要把它当作标记值。

cues.en: For example, if you have a country column, don't use null to mean The United States.
cues.zh: 比如，如果你有一个国家列，不要用 null 表示美国。

cues.en: Don't have it have semantic meaning.
cues.zh: 不要让它带有语义含义。

cues.en: If you have a flag value, create a flag value and use that instead. Only use it to mean...
cues.zh: 如果你需要标记值，就创建一个标记值来表示。只用 null 表示……

cues.en: Because there are lots and lots and lots of times that null will trip you up if you think... If you're using it as a meaningful thing...
cues.zh: 因为很多很多时候，如果你把 null 当作有意义的值……它就会让你栽跟头。

cues.en: Value.
cues.zh: 值。

cues.en: For example,
cues.zh: 举个例子，

cues.en: if you do where not in select and anything in here returns null,
cues.zh: 如果你在查询里用了 WHERE NOT IN，而其中任何一项返回了 NULL，

cues.en: this whole thing will return false,
cues.zh: 整个表达式都会返回 false，

cues.en: which can be really surprising. And that's just one example of how broken null is.
cues.zh: 这可能会让人很意外。这只是 NULL 有多糟糕的一个例子。

cues.en: Okay.
cues.zh: 好。

cues.en: JSON.
cues.zh: JSON。

cues.en: Yay. We have JSON in Postgres. It's better in our... And we do it and we do it better than MongoDB,
cues.zh: 太棒了，Postgres 支持 JSON。在这方面，我们做得更好……我们的实现比 MongoDB 更好，

cues.en: if I do say so myself.
cues.zh: 至少我自己是这么说的。

cues.en: JSON was introduced semi recently in Postgres. It's a core type.
cues.zh: Postgres 不久前引入了 JSON。它是核心类型。

cues.en: It's not a contributor and extension module. You don't have to install it. It just is.
cues.zh: 它不是贡献者维护的扩展模块。不用安装，它本来就在。

cues.en: It was first introduced in nine point two, so it's been around for a while.
cues.zh: 它最早是在 9.2 版本中引入的，所以已经有一段时间了。

cues.en: It was enhanced in 09/03, and it was really enhanced in nine four.
cues.zh: 它在 09/03 得到了改进，在 9.4 版本中更是大幅增强。

cues.en: And we like JSON so much we created two separate types for it. There's JSON and JSONB.
cues.zh: 我们太喜欢 JSON 了，所以专门为它创建了两种类型：JSON 和 JSONB。

cues.en: JSON is a pure text representation.
cues.zh: JSON 是纯文本表示。

cues.en: It
cues.zh: 它

cues.en: is actually really just a wrapper around the text type.
cues.zh: 实际上就是文本类型的一个包装器。

cues.en: You know? So... And JSONB is a parsed binary representation. It's kinda like BSON, only better.
cues.zh: 你知道吧？所以……JSONB 是解析后的二进制表示。它有点像 BSON，不过更好。

cues.en: You can cast one to the other, of course.
cues.zh: 当然可以把其中一个转换成另一个。

cues.en: You know, they... They're freely convertible between the two of them. So the so the
cues.zh: 你知道，它们可以自由地相互转换。所以这两种类型可以自由转换。

cues.en: JSON type was the original one, and it stores the actual JSON text, white space and all.
cues.zh: JSON 类型是最初的类型，它会原样存储实际的 JSON 文本，包括空白字符。

cues.en: The actual JSON blob, it gets in and stored exactly the way it's it's parsed and checked for correctness,
cues.zh: 实际的 JSON 数据块会按解析和校验后的原样存储，

cues.en: but otherwise, it's not processed.
cues.zh: 除此之外不会经过处理。

cues.en: So what you get out is what you get in.
cues.zh: 所以输入什么，取出来就是什么。

cues.en: So why would you use this one? If you're storing the JSON but never processing it,
cues.zh: 那为什么要用这种类型？如果你只是存储 JSON，从不处理它，

cues.en: it's a little faster to insert than JSONB,
cues.zh: 插入速度会比 JSONB 稍快一些，

cues.en: unless you have a crazy amount of white space or something.
cues.zh: 除非里面有特别多的空白字符之类的。

cues.en: Also,
cues.zh: 此外，

cues.en: sometimes you need to... There are two features, and notice these are in scare quotes,
cues.zh: 有时候你还需要……有两个特性，注意这里我加了双引号，

cues.en: that you need to support.
cues.zh: 是你必须要支持的。

cues.en: Order preserved fields and objects. So you have an object with a
cues.zh: 那就是对象中的字段保序。比如你有一个包含 a

cues.en: and b, and they go in as a and b, and you expect them to come out in that order.
cues.zh: 和 b 的对象，输入顺序是 a 然后是 b，你就期望输出也是这个顺序。

cues.en: The JSON spec does not say this is a
cues.zh: JSON 规范并没有说这是

cues.en: feature of JSON,
cues.zh: JSON 的特性，

cues.en: but some APIs expect it, which is really dumb.
cues.zh: 但有些 API 偏偏依赖这个，这真的很蠢。

cues.en: The other one is duplicate keys at the same level in objects. So you have two keys
cues.zh: 另一个特性是对象同级中的重复键。比如在同一个顶层对象里

cues.en: a at the same top level object. Again, the JSON spec doesn't say this is supported, but some APIs expect that.
cues.zh: 有两个键都是 a。同样，JSON 规范并没说支持这个，但有些 API 就吃这一套。

cues.en: Or for some reason you need the exact JSON text back out white space at all. For example, for auditing or forensic purposes, like you're auditing an API and you want to see exactly what came in, words and all.
cues.zh: 或者，你出于某种原因需要原样取回 JSON 文本，连空格都不能有任何变化。比如出于审计或取证目的，你在审计某个 API，想准确查看收到的内容，包括每个字。

cues.en: Or
cues.zh: 或者

cues.en: you're running on nine three and earlier,
cues.zh: 你运行的是 9.3 或更早版本，

cues.en: so JSONB wasn't introduced.
cues.zh: 所以当时还没有引入 JSONB。

cues.en: Otherwise, you generally want to use JSONB. JSONB is parsed and encoded on the way in. It's stored in a compact format. It's a
cues.zh: 除此之外，通常应该使用 JSONB。JSONB 在写入时会被解析和编码，并以紧凑格式存储。它是一种

cues.en: binary format that's parsed.
cues.zh: 经过解析的二进制格式。

cues.en: There's a lot more operator and function support and specifically more indexing support. I'm going to talk a lot more about this. I'm giving a talk about
cues.zh: 它支持了更多的操作符和函数，尤其是提供了更丰富的索引支持。稍后我会详细展开，我还有一场关于

cues.en: Django features
cues.zh: Django 新特性的演讲，

cues.en: in Django
cues.zh: 涵盖 Django

cues.en: and I talk more about indexing JSON.
cues.zh: 到时会深入聊聊 JSON 索引。

cues.en: So very large objects. Let's call a very large object a megabyte or more.
cues.zh: 再来看超大对象，比如 1 MB 及以上的对象。

cues.en: Postgres will
cues.zh: Postgres 存这些

cues.en: store this stuff just fine. You can have a single column value in Postgres can be up to a gigabyte.
cues.zh: 完全没问题。在 Postgres 中，单个列的值最大可以达到 1 GB。

cues.en: Works great.
cues.zh: 效果很棒。

cues.en: Well, for some definitions of great.
cues.zh: 不过嘛，得看你怎么定义“很棒”。

cues.en: For example, you can have a byte a and jump a one... A a 512 megabyte image in that, and Postgres will heroically store that for you.
cues.zh: 比如，你可以有一个字节 a，然后跳过一个……把一个 512 MB 的图像文件塞进去，Postgres 会很卖力地替你存下来。

cues.en: Don't do that.
cues.zh: 别这么做。

cues.en: Store the metadata in the in the database and then store the actual data in a file.
cues.zh: 把元数据存进数据库，然后把实际数据存进文件。

cues.en: I like to say that every modern operating systems ships with a database that is optimized for storing large objects. It's called the file system.
cues.zh: 我喜欢说，每个现代操作系统都自带一个专为存储大型对象优化的数据库，它叫文件系统。

cues.en: So use that.
cues.zh: 就这么用。

cues.en: The database API is just not designed for passing the... For passing these giant objects around.
cues.zh: 数据库 API 并不是为传递……为传递这些庞大的对象而设计的。

cues.en: Many to many tables. Now everyone... You gotta use these in a variety of cases,
cues.zh: 多对多表。现在你得在各种场景中使用它们，

cues.en: but be aware they can get extremely large. You know, the social media problem of you have a million users and a billion things and you need to store likes,
cues.zh: 但要注意，它们可能会变得特别大。比如社交媒体场景：你有一百万个用户和十亿条内容，还得存储点赞，

cues.en: and you store them as a many to many table.
cues.zh: 你会把它们存成一张多对多表。

cues.en: That could be a really big many to many table. So don't do that.
cues.zh: 那张多对多表可能会非常大。所以别这么做。

cues.en: Postgres has array fields as first class objects, and now in JSON at least, they're supported.
cues.zh: Postgres 把数组字段作为一等对象，现在至少在 JSON 中也支持它们。

cues.en: Or in... Not in JSON. In Django, they're supported as real things. They're often... This is often a better way of storing many to many data.
cues.zh: 或者说……不是在 JSON 中。在 Django 里，它们是受支持的真正类型。它们通常……这种方式往往更适合存储多对多数据。

cues.en: Instead of storing... Having a many to many table, for example, you would have who likes this thing stored as an array on the object and what I like stored as an array on the user.
cues.zh: 比如，不用多对多关联表，而是在对象上用数组存储喜欢它的人，在用户上用数组存储我喜欢的东西。

cues.en: You can go either way or both directions.
cues.zh: 你可以选择任一方向，也可以两个方向都选。

cues.en: If you're worried about maintaining integrity,
cues.zh: 如果你担心数据完整性，

cues.en: you can write a trigger that maintains integrity so that they're recorded on both sides.
cues.zh: 可以写一个触发器来维护完整性，让数据同时记录在两边。

cues.en: It's much smaller and more efficient.
cues.zh: 这样体积小得多，也更高效。

cues.en: Of course, a lot of this depends on what your usage model is, what questions you're asking the database.
cues.zh: 当然，这很大程度上取决于你的使用场景，以及你要向数据库查询什么。

cues.en: But be aware that many to many tables can bloat really, really fast.
cues.zh: 但要注意，多对多关系表的体积可能会膨胀得非常快。

cues.en: Character encoding. Let me bang on you once more about character encoding. Use UTF-eight. Just do it. There's really no compelling reason to use any other character encoding now.
cues.zh: 字符编码。再跟你强调一次字符编码：用 UTF-8，就这么做。现在实在没有充分理由使用其他字符编码。

cues.en: You know, people can argue and often correctly about the problems with UTF eight and Unicode, but it's unlikely we're ever getting a better solution in our lifetimes, so just use it. There's one edge case.
cues.zh: 你知道，人们可以争论并且常常正确地指出UTF-8和Unicode的问题，但在我们有生之年不太可能找到更好的解决方案，所以直接用就好了。有一个边缘情况。

cues.en: If you are only storing seven bit ASCII strings
cues.zh: 如果你只存储七位ASCII字符串

cues.en: and the bottleneck on the database is sorting them,
cues.zh: 而且数据库的瓶颈在于对它们排序，

cues.en: that SQL ASCII is faster. But I've only encountered this once in my entire time doing Postgres, so it's a fairly unusual circumstance. So just use UTF-eight.
cues.zh: 那么SQL ASCII更快。但在我使用Postgres的整个经历中只遇到过一次这种情况，所以这是相当罕见的情形。所以直接用UTF-8就好了。

cues.en: Time representation.
cues.zh: 时间表示。

cues.en: Always use timestamp TZ.
cues.zh: 始终使用 timestamp TZ。

cues.en: Never use timestamp.
cues.zh: 永远不要用 timestamp。

cues.en: The
cues.zh: 这个

cues.en: full name of timestamp TZ is timestamp with time zone, which implies that it's bigger than a timestamp. It's not. It's exactly the same size. They're both eight bytes.
cues.zh: timestamp TZ 的全称是 timestamp with time zone，这暗示它比 timestamp 大。其实不是。它们大小完全相同，都是 8 个字节。

cues.en: Timestamp means it's a timestamp, but I know for a fact it's in UTC.
cues.zh: timestamp 意思是它是个时间戳，但我明确知道它是 UTC 时间。

cues.en: And it's converted to UTC on the way in and out for you.
cues.zh: 而且进出时都会帮你转换成 UTC。

cues.en: Timestamp is... It's a timestamp, but we don't know what timestamp it is. What time zone it is, hope you do,
cues.zh: timestamp 是……它是个时间戳，但我们不知道它是哪个时区的时间戳。希望你自己清楚，

cues.en: which can be a really big problem
cues.zh: 这可能是个很大的问题

cues.en: the first time two pieces of your application disagree about what time zone it's in.
cues.zh: 尤其是当应用的两个部分第一次对时区产生分歧的时候。

cues.en: Well,
cues.zh: 嗯，

cues.en: everything's associated with a particular time zone. So local
cues.zh: 所有东西都关联着一个特定的时区。所以本地……

cues.en: I'm not even sure quite what you mean there.
cues.zh: 我也不太确定你具体指什么。

cues.en: So you're saying time zone is the
cues.zh: 所以你是说，时区就是……

cues.en: same time zone associated with
cues.zh: 关联到同一个时区……

cues.en: It doesn't, actually. Well, does, but that time zone is always UTC.
cues.zh: 其实不是。嗯，也算是，但那个时区始终是 UTC。

cues.en: Yeah. So... Yeah. So what Postgres will do is the... Will con... Will take...
cues.zh: 对。所以……对。Postgres 会做的是……会……会把……

cues.en: If you send in a time stamp TZ and the the representation
cues.zh: 如果你传入一个带时区的时间戳，而它的表示形式

cues.en: of that shows a different time zone, it'll convert it to UTC for you
cues.zh: 显示的是另一个时区，它就会帮你转换成 UTC，

cues.en: and then convert it back out on the way out.
cues.zh: 然后取出时再转换回去。

cues.en: So just always use time stamp TC because a time stamp without a time zone is effectively meaningless. So somebody somewhere needs to know what time stamp... Time zone it is, so you might as well associate it. We have the database keep track of it.
cues.zh: 所以尽量总是使用带时区的时间戳（timestamptz），因为没有时区的时间戳实际上毫无意义。总有人、总有地方需要知道它具体是……哪个时区，所以不妨把它关联起来。直接让数据库来记录它。

cues.en: Okay.
cues.zh: 好的。

cues.en: Indexing.
cues.zh: 索引。

cues.en: Everyone's favorite topic about databases,
cues.zh: 大家在数据库领域最喜欢的话题，

cues.en: sort of.
cues.zh: 大概算吧。

cues.en: So
cues.zh: 那么，

cues.en: pop pop quiz. What does the SQL standard require for indexes?
cues.zh: 突击测验：SQL 标准对索引有什么要求？

cues.en: Trick question.
cues.zh: 这是个陷阱题。

cues.en: It doesn't mention indexes at all. There is no reference in the SQL standard indexes. They don't exist. Not... The
cues.zh: 它压根没提索引。SQL 标准里没有任何关于索引的参考说明。它们根本不存在。不……

cues.en: reason is they're considered a performance optimization
cues.zh: 原因在于它们被视为一种性能优化，

cues.en: is the database should work correctly
cues.zh: 数据库应当正常运行，

cues.en: or or identically
cues.zh: 或者说结果保持一致，

cues.en: whether you... Now you have indexes. In this case, identically, of course, doesn't mean much... Just as fast. It means you just get the same data out.
cues.zh: 无论你……现在有没有建索引。当然，这里的“一致”并不是指……速度一样快，而是指你查出的数据完全相同。

cues.en: No real life system can work
cues.zh: 没有任何现实中的系统能够运转

cues.en: without indexes.
cues.zh: 没有索引。

cues.en: PostgresQL
cues.zh: PostgresQL

cues.en: has an embarrassment of riches on index types. Right now we have btree,
cues.zh: 在索引类型上简直多到让人挑花眼。目前我们有 btree，

cues.en: hash, which we're not going to talk about because it's not really well implemented in Postgres,
cues.zh: 哈希索引，这个我们就不细讲了，因为在 Postgres 里的实现其实不太成熟，

cues.en: gist,
cues.zh: gist,

cues.en: SPGIST, which we're not gonna talk about because it's not very... They're not... There's not a lot of type support for it, and GIN. So we're gonna talk about b tree, gist, and GIN indexes.
cues.zh: SPGIST，我们不打算讲它，因为它不太……它们不太……对它的类型支持不多，还有GIN。所以我们要讲的是b树、gist和GIN索引。

cues.en: So people are basically familiar with b trees as a data structure. Interestingly enough, no one knows why they're called b trees. There's no history of why they're called b trees. The general thing is they're either... It's either for balanced or Boeing
cues.zh: 所以大家基本都熟悉 B 树这种数据结构。有意思的是，没人知道它为什么叫 B 树，也没有相关的命名历史。一般的说法是，它要么……要么是因为“平衡”（balanced），要么是因为“波音”（Boeing）

cues.en: because the people... The guys who invented it were engineers at Boeing.
cues.zh: 因为……发明 B 树的人是波音公司的工程师。

cues.en: B It's trees are great. They provide order log in access to leaf nodes. They provide total ordering.
cues.zh: B 树很棒。它能以对数时间访问叶节点，还能提供全序关系。

cues.en: They operate on scalar values that implement the standard comparison operators. So they have... So b... You can index a column that's a standard... That can be compared as greater than, less than, or equal to.
cues.zh: 它们针对的是实现了标准比较运算符的标量值。所以它们有……所以 B……你可以为那些标准的……可以进行大于、小于或等于比较的列建立索引。

cues.en: Not every type in the world can be compared in that way, and for those we have other index types.
cues.zh: 但并非所有类型都能这样比较，针对那些类型，我们有其他的索引类型。

cues.en: B trees can come in a single column, multiple column or composite indexes,
cues.zh: B 树索引可以是单列索引、多列或复合索引，

cues.en: or expression or functional indexes.
cues.zh: 也可以是表达式索引或函数索引。

cues.en: A single column B tree,
cues.zh: 单列 B 树，

cues.en: which is the simplest index type,
cues.zh: 它是最简单的索引类型，

cues.en: optimizes searches on the standard comparison operators,
cues.zh: 优化标准比较运算符上的搜索，

cues.en: and it can be used to retrieve rows in sorted order on that column. So sometimes you'll be able to use an index instead of having to sort, which is really, really nice.
cues.zh: 它还可以用来按该列的排序顺序检索行。所以有时你可以直接利用索引，而无需额外排序，这真的非常棒。

cues.en: So when do you want to create one of these?
cues.zh: 那什么时候该创建一个呢？

cues.en: You know, speaking... I I read a lot of Django code, and I see a lot of DB index equals true.
cues.zh: 你知道吗，说起来……我读过很多 Django 代码，经常看到一大堆 DB index equals true。

cues.en: And they said, well, what... Why is that index there? And they say, well, I thought I might want a query on it sometime. And so you'll see a call... An index... A table with, like, 18 indexes on it, and inserting in that... On... Into that table takes a long, long time.
cues.zh: 他们会问：“呃，为什么这里有个索引？”然后回答说：“哦，我觉得以后可能会查这个字段。”所以你会看到一个……一张表上建了大概 18 个索引，结果往这张表里插入数据变得奇慢无比。

cues.en: Roughly speaking,
cues.zh: 大致来说，

cues.en: each index takes as long to insert into as it does to insert into the primary call index structure. So if you have 18 indexes, it takes 18 times as long
cues.zh: 向每个索引插入数据所花的时间，跟向主索引结构插入差不多。所以如果你有 18 个索引，耗时就会变成原来的 18 倍，

cues.en: to insert a call... A row.
cues.zh: 只为了插入一条……一行数据。

cues.en: So maybe it's not always worth it.
cues.zh: 所以可能并不总是值得建索引。

cues.en: So the the way you decide if it's worth it is, first of all, query has to use that column. There's no point in indexing something that you never query on. And use one of the comparison operators.
cues.zh: 判断它是否值得的方法是：首先，查询必须用到该列。给从不查询的列建索引毫无意义。并且要使用某种比较运算符。

cues.en: And
cues.zh: 而且，

cues.en: this is the big one. The query selects less than 10 to 15% of the rows.
cues.zh: 最关键的一点是：查询筛选出的数据量要少于总行数的 10% 到 15%。

cues.en: So if you have a 5,000,000 row table,
cues.zh: 所以，如果你有一张 500 万行的表，

cues.en: if your query is gonna select 3,000,000 of those rows,
cues.zh: 而你的查询要选出其中的 300 万行，

cues.en: an index won't help you. Postgres almost certainly will not even use the index.
cues.zh: 索引就帮不上什么忙了。Postgres 几乎肯定根本不会去走索引。

cues.en: Lastly, it's run frequently.
cues.zh: 最后，它会被频繁执行。

cues.en: Basically, you want the query to be run often enough that you're trading off the cost of...
cues.zh: 基本上，你要让查询运行得足够频繁，这样才值得权衡……的成本。

cues.en: Extra cost of insert.
cues.zh: 插入带来的额外成本。

cues.en: You know, if this is a query that's run once a month to do summarization,
cues.zh: 你知道，如果这个查询每月只运行一次，用来做汇总，

cues.en: maybe you don't need an index on it. Maybe the fact that it takes a long time is okay.
cues.zh: 那可能就不需要给它建索引。耗时比较长也没关系。

cues.en: If all of these are true, the index is likely to be helpful.
cues.zh: 如果这些条件都成立，索引很可能会有帮助。

cues.en: Indexes can accelerate joins,
cues.zh: 索引可以加速联接，

cues.en: but the same rules apply.
cues.zh: 但同样的规则也适用。

cues.en: The joins... The the the index has to... The one side has to be 10 to 15% of the total table.
cues.zh: 连接……索引……那一侧必须占整张表的 10% 到 15%。

cues.en: Generally,
cues.zh: 一般来说，

cues.en: they help the most when you're... When the indexing the key on the larger table, and that results in high selectivity against the smaller table. Selectivity is that 10 to 15% number. High selectivity is a small percentage in that.
cues.zh: 它们在……当你在较大的表上给键建索引，并且这能对较小的表产生高选择性时，帮助最大。选择性就是那个 10% 到 15% 的数字。高选择性指的是其中很小的百分比。

cues.en: Indexes can... Some group buying related operations can benefit from an index. Indexes are implicitly grouped already,
cues.zh: 索引可以……一些与团购相关的操作能从索引中受益。索引本身已经是隐式分组的，

cues.en: if you think about it, because it compresses... If you have 15 things
cues.zh: 仔细想想，因为它会压缩……如果你有 15 个东西

cues.en: are all... That all have the same value... Rows that all have the same value in index, those will all be compressed together into similar index pages. So they can be used to accelerate GROUP BY,
cues.zh: 全都……全都具有相同的值……索引中值相同的那些行，都会被压缩进相似的索引页里。所以它们可以用来加速 GROUP BY，

cues.en: but generally you need a having clause in Postgres and very few queries, especially those generated by ORMs, use the having clause in SQL.
cues.zh: 但一般来说，在 Postgres 中你需要一个 having 子句，而很少有查询——尤其是那些由 ORM 生成的查询——会在 SQL 中使用 having 子句。

cues.en: Important thing to remember is if it has to scan the whole index, it might as well scan the the bay... The underlying table because it's much faster to scan the table than it is to scan an index.
cues.zh: 重要的是要记住，如果必须全索引扫描，那还不如直接扫描……底层的表，因为全表扫描要比扫描索引快得多。

cues.en: Because walking index is quite expensive because bouncing around through this page structure is
cues.zh: 因为遍历索引非常昂贵，在这些页面结构之间来回跳跃

cues.en: expensive both in computation and in IO.
cues.zh: 无论是计算开销还是 I/O 开销都很大。

cues.en: Sometimes... There's sometimes you have to have an index. For example, if you have a primary key, it has to have an index to enforce it in Postgres, and you just accept those. You know?
cues.zh: 有时……有时你必须建索引。比如主键，在 Postgres 中必须有索引来约束，这种情况你只能接受，对吧？

cues.en: You can create an index as either ascending or descending in Postgres.
cues.zh: 在 Postgres 中，你可以创建升序或降序的索引。

cues.en: By default, they work in ascending order.
cues.zh: 默认情况下，它们按升序工作。

cues.en: Descending indexes are much faster if you're retrieving the tuples in descending order. So if the primary function is to sort tuples in descending order, for example, you're going to do a query with a small limit value,
cues.zh: 如果你按降序检索元组，降序索引会快得多。所以，如果主要功能是按降序排列元组，例如，你要执行一个带有较小 limit 值的查询，

cues.en: and that'll frequently use an index,
cues.zh: 而这经常会用到索引，

cues.en: It
cues.zh: 那

cues.en: might make sense to create the index in descending order. Otherwise, just accept it ascending order.
cues.zh: 创建降序索引可能就是合理的。否则，就用升序就行了。

cues.en: You can also have composite indexes in Postgres.
cues.zh: 在 Postgres 中你也可以使用复合索引。

cues.en: One catch on composite indexes is that you have to use left to right. So you can create an index on a, b, and c, but it doesn't help you at all for queries on c.
cues.zh: 复合索引需要注意的一点是，你必须从左到右来使用它。比如你在 a、b、c 上建了索引，但它对单独查询 c 完全没有帮助。

cues.en: But it will help you for queries on a, b. You don't have to use all of them, but if you do use them, you have to use them left to right. So you can do a query it'll help with queries on A and queries on A and B, but it won't help at all for queries on B and C by themselves.
cues.zh: 但它对查询 a、b 是有帮助的。你不必使用所有列，但如果要用，就必须从左到右去用。所以它能加速针对 a 的查询，以及针对 a 和 b 的查询，但对只查 b 和 c 的查询完全起不到作用。

cues.en: Base this on what kind of queries you actually do.
cues.zh: 这取决于你实际执行的查询类型。

cues.en: One feature of Postgres most ORMs don't support this, you have to create them manually is expression indexes.
cues.zh: Postgres 的一个特性是表达式索引，大多数 ORM 都不支持，你必须手动创建。

cues.en: So for example,
cues.zh: 举个例子，

cues.en: can create an index on an expression,
cues.zh: 你可以针对一个表达式创建索引，

cues.en: not on a specific column.
cues.zh: 而不是针对某个具体的列。

cues.en: And Postgres will recognize when you're using that expression in the query
cues.zh: 当你在查询中使用该表达式时，Postgres 能够识别出来，

cues.en: and and use the index instead. A very common use for this is queries on lower text column.
cues.zh: 进而去使用这个索引。一个非常常见的用法是在 lower(text_column) 上做查询。

cues.en: You can create an index on lower text column, and then when you query on lower text column, Postgres will use that index.
cues.zh: 你可以在转换为小写的文本列上创建索引，这样查询该列时，Postgres 就会使用这个索引。

cues.en: So, for example, for case insensitive searching.
cues.zh: 比如，用于不区分大小写的搜索。

cues.en: They can be expensive to create because
cues.zh: 创建这类索引可能成本很高，因为

cues.en: it has to run this function for each row, but they can really help for things where you have to use a query... Where you have to use an expression in the query.
cues.zh: 它必须对每一行运行这个函数。不过，对于查询中必须使用表达式的场景，这类索引确实很有帮助。

cues.en: But make sure Postgres is really using it.
cues.zh: 不过要确认 Postgres 确实在使用这个索引。

cues.en: We'll talk about how... Mhmm?
cues.zh: 我们会聊聊怎么……嗯？

cues.en: It's stored as an index. Yeah. It's it's just like any other index once you've created it. And Postgres automatically updates it as the rows update and things like that.
cues.zh: 它是作为索引存储的。对，一旦创建好，它就和普通索引没两样。Postgres 会在行更新等情况下自动更新它。

cues.en: Another feature that's not used enough, I think, in Postgres is a is a partial index. You can create an index that doesn't contain all of the rows.
cues.zh: 我认为 Postgres 里另一个未被充分利用的特性是部分索引（partial index）。你可以创建一个并不包含所有行的索引。

cues.en: You slap a clause called a when clause or a predicate
cues.zh: 只要加上一个叫 when 的子句，也就是谓词，

cues.en: onto the index onto the index creation statement,
cues.zh: 加到索引创建语句中，

cues.en: and that limits the size of the index. For example, let's say you had an order table and it had an active flag that says it's an active order. You can say, well, I want to create a row,
cues.zh: 就能限制索引的大小。比如，假设你有一个订单表，里面有个 active 标记表示它是一个活跃订单。你可以说，我想创建一行，

cues.en: an index on
cues.zh: 在……上建一个索引，

cues.en: something about
cues.zh: 针对订单的

cues.en: the order when active.
cues.zh: 某些字段，当 active 为真时生效。

cues.en: And then if I did a query that was
cues.zh: 如果我执行这样一个查询：

cues.en: look for orders when active and,
cues.zh: 查找 active 状态的订单，并且……

cues.en: it would use that index. And that index potentially is much smaller and so the query runs much faster.
cues.zh: 它就会走那个索引。而且那个索引可能小得多，查询速度也就会快得多。

cues.en: So if
cues.zh: 所以如果

cues.en: the predicate greatly reduces the size of the index
cues.zh: 谓词条件能大幅缩减索引大小，

cues.en: and you frequently query using that predicate,
cues.zh: 而你又经常用这个谓词来查询，

cues.en: this can be a very big performance win.
cues.zh: 这就能带来巨大的性能提升。

cues.en: One thing to note is index
cues.zh: 需要注意的一点是，索引

cues.en: is MVCC.
cues.zh: 也是受 MVCC 影响的。

cues.en: The whole key value is copied into the index.
cues.zh: 完整的键值都会被复制到索引中。

cues.en: And every version of the tuple on disk appears in the index, which means that Postgres needs to go out into the database to check if they're live or not,
cues.zh: 磁盘上元组的每个版本都会出现在索引里，这意味着 Postgres 必须回表去检查它们是否有效，

cues.en: see if they're visible.
cues.zh: 看看它们是否可见。

cues.en: One of the things is that this means indexes can bloat the same way tables can bloat.
cues.zh: 其中一点是，这意味着索引也会像表一样发生膨胀。

cues.en: Vacuum does reclaim the data from the indexes, but because indexes have more structure, they will tend to be a little larger
cues.zh: Vacuum 确实会从索引中回收数据，但因为索引结构更复杂，它们往往会稍大一些

cues.en: than they would otherwise because it can't reclaim as much space.
cues.zh: 因为它能回收的空间没那么多，所以比平时更……

cues.en: Okay.
cues.zh: 好的。

cues.en: So
cues.zh: 所以

cues.en: that's great if you're indexing on things like
cues.zh: 如果你看重的是像这样的指标，那确实很棒

cues.en: text strings and integers and time stamps and things that were greater than or less than or equal to work.
cues.zh: 文本、整数、时间戳，以及大于、小于、等于之类的运算，都能正常工作。

cues.en: But what about points
cues.zh: 但如果是点

cues.en: and rectangles
cues.zh: 矩形

cues.en: and things like that? Because they're...
cues.zh: 之类的几何对象呢？因为它们……

cues.en: You you know, it doesn't make any sense to say one point is greater than or less than another point.
cues.zh: 你知道，说一个点大于或小于另一个点是毫无意义的。

cues.en: For those, we have GIST indexes.
cues.zh: 对于这类数据，我们有 GiST 索引。

cues.en: GIST isn't a single index type. It's actually a framework for building your own indexes. You can use it to create B tree style indexes, but what it's usually used for is create indexes for like bounding box and geometric queries,
cues.zh: GiST 并不是单一的索引类型。它实际上是一个用于构建自定义索引的框架。你可以用它创建 B-tree 风格的索引，但它最常用于为边界框和几何查询创建索引，

cues.en: for things like indexing a bunch of rectangles and then saying, find me all the rectangles that this point is in,
cues.zh: 比如索引一堆矩形，然后查询包含某个点的所有矩形，

cues.en: like geometric queries.
cues.zh: 也就是几何查询这类场景。

cues.en: Generally, if you have a type that's not totally ordered, like a point or rectangle or geometries of that kind or ranges,
cues.zh: 一般来说，如果你的类型不是全序的，比如点、矩形、这类几何类型，或者范围，

cues.en: you need to need a gist index.
cues.zh: 你就需要一个 GIST 索引。

cues.en: One of the things that's complicated about gist indexes is you have to say, well,
cues.zh: GIST 索引有个复杂之处：你得弄清楚，

cues.en: what operators does this particular type support, and which ones does the GIST index accelerate? And that's something just you have to open the documentation and read. You know? So for example,
cues.zh: 这个类型支持哪些运算符，哪些运算符能由 GIST 索引加速？这就得打开文档仔细看了。比如说，

cues.en: inclusion or membership or containment or intersection
cues.zh: 包含、成员关系、包容或相交

cues.en: are the kinds of things that GIST tends to
cues.zh: 这些通常都是 GIST

cues.en: support. And some GIST indexes do provide ordering for types that make sense to to talk about ordering.
cues.zh: 支持的操作。有些 GIST 索引也支持有序类型的排序。

cues.en: Specifically, there's a
cues.zh: 具体来说，有一种

cues.en: GIST index type called KNN for nearest neighbor,
cues.zh: 名为 KNN 的 GIST 索引类型，用于最近邻查询，

cues.en: for k th nearest neighbor, which finally solves the Starbucks problem, which is actually real... Which is a classic geometric
cues.zh: 即第 k 近邻，它终于解决了星巴克问题，这问题其实真实存在……这是一个经典的几何

cues.en: database problem, which is actually kind of hard to solve, which is find me the nearest 10 Starbucks to this point.
cues.zh: 数据库问题，实际上相当难解，也就是找出离这个点最近的 10 家星巴克。

cues.en: And you think, well, if a geometric database... If a...
cues.zh: 你会想，好吧，如果一个几何数据库……如果一个……

cues.en: If, you know, geographic
cues.zh: 如果，你知道，地理

cues.en: database is good for anything, it's for finding Starbucks. Right? You know? But that's actually kind of hard because if your only operation is what points are near this point?
cues.zh: 数据库有什么用处的话，那应该是找星巴克吧？对吧？你知道吗？但这其实挺难的，因为如果你唯一的操作是“哪些点在这点附近？”

cues.en: Well, first of all, how many points do we search? Do we search across every
cues.zh: 首先，我们要搜索多少个点？是要把全世界的

cues.en: Starbucks in the entire world and then sort them? Well, that doesn't make much sense. Okay. How about you say, no. We won't do that. We're gonna draw a a 10 mile rectangle.
cues.zh: 每家星巴克都搜一遍然后排序吗？这显然不太合理。那好吧，你说不这么干，我们画一个 10 英里的矩形框。

cues.en: Well, that's great. In, you know, in Portland, probably a three... A two mile port...
cues.zh: 这想法不错。但在波特兰，可能画一个三……两英里的……

cues.en: Square will be fine. But if you're the middle of Montana,
cues.zh: 正方形就足够了。但如果你是在蒙大拿州中部，

cues.en: probably a 100 mile rectangle is required. And that's a hard problem. Fortunately, K and N indexes just solve that problem for you. So check the docs. They're great.
cues.zh: 可能就需要画一个 100 英里的矩形。这是个棘手的问题。好在 KNN 索引正好能帮你解决这个问题。去看看文档吧，写得非常棒。

cues.en: Okay.
cues.zh: 好的。

cues.en: The last index type is called a gin index. It's for generalized inverted index. Although,
cues.zh: 最后一种索引类型叫做 GIN 索引，即通用倒排索引（Generalized Inverted Index）。不过，

cues.en: it's interestingly enough, the crazy Russians who came up with the gin index also have a vodka and rum index, so maybe gin is not what they were thinking of.
cues.zh: 挺有意思的是，想出 GIN 索引的那些疯狂俄罗斯人，还搞出了 Vodka 和 Rum 索引，所以 GIN 可能并不是指我们想的那种金酒。

cues.en: It's an inverted index, which is a classic, like, the index in a back of a book kind of index, is it maps keywords to rows that contain tokens,
cues.zh: 它是一种倒排索引，非常经典，就像书本末尾的那种索引一样，它把关键字映射到包含这些 Token 的行，

cues.en: like keywords,
cues.zh: 比如把关键字，

cues.en: to rows that contain those keywords.
cues.zh: 映射到包含这些关键字的行。

cues.en: The full text search functionality in Postgres uses GIN indexes.
cues.zh: Postgres 中的全文搜索功能使用的是 GIN 索引。

cues.en: So
cues.zh: 所以，

cues.en: it's a classic index design for you have a set of things and you want to say,
cues.zh: 这是一种经典的索引设计，适用于你有一组数据，并且你想说：

cues.en: find me everything that has Fred in it.
cues.zh: “帮我找出所有包含 Fred 的内容。”

cues.en: Because in the case of... For the specific use for full text searches, it takes the words and tokenizes them, you know, strips off
cues.zh: 因为具体到全文搜索这个场景，它会提取单词并进行分词，比如去除

cues.en: tense endings and pluralization and normalizes them, and then stores every row,
cues.zh: 时态后缀和复数形式，并将它们归一化，然后存储每一行，

cues.en: every row
cues.zh: 存储包含

cues.en: that has one of those... That token in it.
cues.zh: 其中某个……包含该词元（token）的每一行。

cues.en: It's implemented as a b tree of b trees. The tokens are organized into b trees, the rows pointers are organized into b trees. And what we're getting at here is it can be pretty big on disk.
cues.zh: 它是作为 b 树的 b 树来实现的。token 被组织成 b 树，行指针被组织成 b 树。我们在这里想说的是，它在磁盘上可能相当大。

cues.en: So just be aware that GIN indexes can be pretty large.
cues.zh: 所以要注意，GIN 索引可能会相当大。

cues.en: Although recent versions of Postgres have optimized this considerably.
cues.zh: 不过 Postgres 的近期版本对这一块做了相当大的优化。

cues.en: So the number one question everyone asks is, why isn't it using my index? You know, it's like, you know, you write a query and you run it, and it's slow.
cues.zh: 所以大家问得最多的问题就是，为什么它没用我的索引？你知道，就像你写了个查询然后跑起来，结果很慢。

cues.en: So the first thing to do is... Everyone... Who's familiar with explain analyze in Postgres?
cues.zh: 首先要做的是……大家……有谁熟悉 Postgres 里的 explain analyze？

cues.en: Okay.
cues.zh: 好。

cues.en: Get get used to explain analyze. Well, this is a keyword... These are two keywords you type at the beginning
cues.zh: 慢慢习惯用 explain analyze。这是个关键字……这是你在

cues.en: of a query.
cues.zh: 查询开头要输入的两个关键字。

cues.en: It runs the query and dumps the query plan,
cues.zh: 它会执行查询并输出查询计划，

cues.en: which is horrible and nasty to look at, but is essential for figuring out how to optimize queries. We'll talk a little bit about this in a bit.
cues.zh: 那玩意儿看起来又乱又难受，但对弄清如何优化查询至关重要。我们稍后会稍微聊聊这个。

cues.en: So the answer may be, maybe you might be using the index and the query is just slow anyway.
cues.zh: 所以答案可能是，你确实在用索引，只是查询本身还是很慢。

cues.en: And you find this out from explain analyze because you can see that it's using the index.
cues.zh: 你可以通过 EXPLAIN ANALYZE 发现这一点，因为能看到它正在使用索引。

cues.en: The main reason if it's not using the index is bad selectivity.
cues.zh: 如果没有使用索引，主要原因是选择性太差。

cues.en: Because if Postgres thinks that index will return a large percentage of the table, it'll do a sequential scan instead because that's more efficient.
cues.zh: 因为如果 Postgres 认为索引会返回表中很大一部分数据，就会改用顺序扫描，因为这样更高效。

cues.en: And generally, it's right.
cues.zh: 通常它的判断是对的。

cues.en: If you think it's wrong, try running analyze again
cues.zh: 如果你觉得不对，就再运行一次 analyze

cues.en: so it picks up new planner statistics
cues.zh: 这样它就能获取新的查询规划器统计信息

cues.en: and run the query again.
cues.zh: 然后再次运行查询。

cues.en: Well,
cues.zh: 好吧，

cues.en: analyze didn't help. Still not using the index. You still think it should.
cues.zh: analyze 没起作用。还是没用上索引。你仍然认为它应该用。

cues.en: You can turn off sequential scans.
cues.zh: 你可以关闭顺序扫描。

cues.en: This isn't for the whole system. This is just for... Know, that would be bad. This is just for your your session.
cues.zh: 这不是对整个系统。这只是对……要知道，那会很糟。这只是对你的会话。

cues.en: You issue this command, and now it's... Now it's... Now you've told it, in... Except as the last possible resort,
cues.zh: 你发出这个命令，现在它就……现在它就……现在你告诉它，除非作为最后的手段，

cues.en: don't run a sequential scan.
cues.zh: 否则不要执行顺序扫描。

cues.en: And then see if it uses the index any... Then.
cues.zh: 然后看看它有没有使用这个索引……接着。

cues.en: Because if it doesn't then, the answer is it doesn't think this index applies to this query.
cues.zh: 因为如果没有，那答案就是：它认为这个索引不适用于这个查询。

cues.en: So
cues.zh: 所以……

cues.en: was the query miswritten in some way that it can't use the index? Is the index marked as invalid? That doesn't happen very often, but it can happen. You can see that if you...
cues.zh: 查询是不是写错了，导致它无法使用这个索引？这个索引是不是被标记为无效？这种情况不常见，但也可能发生。你可以这样查看……

cues.en: In in in PSQL, you can... If you type backslash d plus and the name of the table, you... It'll list the table and all the indexes, and it'll say invalid after it, which case you just rebuild the index.
cues.zh: 在 PSQL 里，你可以……输入反斜杠 d 加号，再加上表名，它就会列出这张表和所有索引；如果索引后面显示“无效”，你只要重建索引就行。

cues.en: Are you using expression index and Postgres is confused and doesn't realize the expression index applies?
cues.zh: 你是否用了表达式索引，而 Postgres 犯迷糊了，没意识到该用这个表达式索引？

cues.en: That's another possibility.
cues.zh: 那是另一种可能。

cues.en: Number one thing is try doing a simple query on just that fill... Field and build up your overall query and seeing if you can get it to use it then. Sometimes
cues.zh: 首要的做法是先针对那个字……字段写个简单查询，再逐步构建完整查询，看看那时能否让它用上索引。有时候

cues.en: you'll get the Postgres right but wrong,
cues.zh: 虽然 Postgres 认为不用更好，但它是错的，

cues.en: and you force it to use the index, and in fact the index is actually faster.
cues.zh: 而当你强制它使用索引时，实际上走索引确实更快。

cues.en: And it just generates a bad plan.
cues.zh: 结果就是生成了一个糟糕的计划。

cues.en: This is one thing that lowering random page costs can help with. That tends to encourage it to use the index more.
cues.zh: 这正是降低随机页面成本能帮上忙的一点，它往往会促使规划器更多地使用索引。

cues.en: You can also change the default statistics target for that field. By default, Postgres only keeps a 100 buckets.
cues.zh: 你也可以修改该字段的默认统计目标。默认情况下，Postgres 只保留 100 个桶。

cues.en: It's basically a histogram of values for every column.
cues.zh: 它基本上就是每个列的取值直方图。

cues.en: If you can bump that up to 500 or a thousand, it might have better
cues.zh: 如果你能把它提高到 500 或 1000，它可能就会有更好的

cues.en: insight into how... What's going on there.
cues.zh: 洞察，弄清那里到底……发生了什么。

cues.en: You can create an index on Postgres in a couple of different ways.
cues.zh: 在 Postgres 中创建索引有几种不同的方式。

cues.en: Create index or create index concurrently.
cues.zh: 可以用 create index，或者 create index concurrently。

cues.en: Create index is the standard way. It's the fastest way.
cues.zh: Create index 是标准方式，也是最快的方式。

cues.en: It does a single scan of the table and builds the index, but it has one really bad characteristic.
cues.zh: 它对表进行单次扫描并构建索引，但有一个非常糟糕的特性。

cues.en: It keeps exclusive lock on the table the entire time you're building it, which for a system that's up and running is probably not acceptable because it blocks all access to that table.
cues.zh: 在构建的整个过程中，它都会对表持有排他锁，对于正在运行的生产系统来说，这大概率是无法接受的，因为它会阻塞对该表的所有访问。

cues.en: As an alternative, you can use create index concurrently. It does two passes.
cues.zh: 作为替代方案，你可以使用 create index concurrently。它分两步执行。

cues.en: It builds the index and then validates the index. And if the... This is the number one way of getting an invalid index. If the validation fails,
cues.zh: 先构建索引，然后再进行校验。如果……这是导致索引失效的最主要原因。如果校验失败，

cues.en: it'll...
cues.zh: 它就会……

cues.en: It will be marked as invalid and won't be used. This will happen, for example, if you're creating a unique index using create index concurrently and somebody inserts in a nonunique value while you're doing it.
cues.zh: 它会被标记为无效且不会被使用。比如，当你用 create index concurrently 创建唯一索引时，如果有人在你创建期间插入了一个不唯一的值，就会发生这种情况。

cues.en: So if that happens, just drop it and run it again. Of course, if there's nonunique value, you'll get an error. But
cues.zh: 如果发生这种情况，直接删掉重新执行就行。当然，如果存在不唯一的值，就会报错。不过

cues.en: the the... This takes much longer,
cues.zh: 这……这耗时要长得多，

cues.en: but it it doesn't... It never takes... It only takes exclusive lock on the table for very brief windows.
cues.zh: 但它……它从不……它只会在极短的时间窗口内对表加排他锁。

cues.en: There is also a reindex command you can use to build... Rebuild an index, for example, it gets bloated.
cues.zh: 还有一个 reindex 命令，可以用来构……重建索引，比如在索引膨胀的时候。

cues.en: Unfortunately, it also takes exclusive lock on the table, which is not so great.
cues.zh: 不幸的是，它也会对表加排他锁，这就有点糟糕了。

cues.en: You can... You... The other thing you can do is just drop the... Is just create a new index using create index concurrently
cues.zh: 你可以……你……还有一种做法，就是直接创建一个新的索引，用 `create index concurrently`

cues.en: that's identical to the old one and then drop the old one. So that may be better than doing a reindex.
cues.zh: 让它和旧索引完全一样，然后删掉旧索引。这样可能比重新索引更好。

cues.en: They can be bloated,
cues.zh: 它们可能会变得臃肿，

cues.en: especially sparse deletions can bloat them because you
cues.zh: 尤其是零散的删除会让它们膨胀，因为你

cues.en: delete a bunch of columns
cues.zh: 删除了很多列

cues.en: from within the within the table that have... Are... That are picked out from various
cues.zh: 从表中……表内……这些列分散在各处……

cues.en: points,
cues.zh: 的位置，

cues.en: and new inserts never go into those old holes. So even if it reclaims the space,
cues.zh: 而新插入的数据永远不会填进这些旧空洞。所以即使它回收了空间，

cues.en: as Marx is free, the free space isn't being used by anything.
cues.zh: 就像 Marx is free 一样，这些空闲空间也没有被任何东西利用。

cues.en: Again, don't have to copy this down. It'll be in the notes. There's a script for finding index bloat.
cues.zh: 再次提醒，不用抄这个，笔记里都会有。这里有个脚本可以用来排查索引膨胀。

cues.en: Generally, though, don't worry about it.
cues.zh: 不过一般来说，不用太担心这个。

cues.en: There is a view in Postgres called p g stat user indexes. It works
cues.zh: Postgres 里有一个叫 pg_stat_user_indexes 的视图，用起来

cues.en: just like a table. You say select star from p g stat user indexes.
cues.zh: 就像一张表一样。你直接写 select * from pg_stat_user_indexes 即可。

cues.en: It reports the number of times an index has been used.
cues.zh: 它会汇报某个索引被使用的次数。

cues.en: So it's really handy because you can build an index, run stuff for a while, go in and see if anything's actually using it, and drop it if it's not being used.
cues.zh: 这非常实用，因为你可以建好索引后先跑一段时间，再去看看有没有查询真的在用它，没人用就可以直接删了。

cues.en: And if it's not being used to enforce a constraint like a unique... A primary key,
cues.zh: 如果它不是用来强制执行类似唯一性……主键这种约束，

cues.en: drop indexes that aren't being used
cues.zh: 那就删掉没用到的索引，

cues.en: because they are very expensive to maintain.
cues.zh: 因为维护索引的开销非常大。

cues.en: And again, don't create indexes on columns prospectively.
cues.zh: 再次提醒，不要提前给列建索引。

cues.en: Only create an index if you have
cues.zh: 只有当你遇到

cues.en: a query that's not performing very well, and an index will help perform
cues.zh: 性能不好的查询，而加索引确实能大幅提升性能时，

cues.en: very well. It's really easy to over index a database.
cues.zh: 再去创建。数据库很容易索引过度。

cues.en: Okay.
cues.zh: 好的。

cues.en: Questions on indexing?
cues.zh: 关于索引有什么问题吗？

cues.en: Getting
cues.zh: 快结束了。

cues.en: close to the end.
cues.zh: 快接近尾声了。

cues.en: Yes?
cues.zh: 是吗？

cues.en: Yeah.
cues.zh: 是的。

cues.en: Yeah. There... There's no reason... There... There's no... If you... For... It's... If you have a unique index and a nonunique index, just drop the nonunique index because it... It's not doing anything for you. Similarly, if you have an index on a, b, c, there's no point in having an index on a also.
cues.zh: 对。没理由……如果……有唯一索引和非唯一索引，直接删掉非唯一索引，因为它对你毫无用处。同样，如果在 a、b、c 上有索引，再在 a 上单独建索引就没意义了。

cues.en: And so the unique index...
cues.zh: 所以唯一索引……

cues.en: Sure. You betcha. They'll be used anytime it uses another index.
cues.zh: 当然，没问题。只要用到其他索引时，它们就会被用上。

cues.en: It it would... It needs an index for that column. Nothing. Best type of index. Well,
cues.zh: 它会……这列需要建索引。没有。最好的索引类型，嗯，

cues.en: it's great if you... If the column's unique.
cues.zh: 要是这一列是唯一列，那就太棒了。

cues.en: You know? It's
cues.zh: 懂吧？对 Postgres 来说，

cues.en: no more work for Postgres to enforce a unique index than it is for any other index because it has to do the insert into the index anyway. Just the result is it'll throw an error if it finds the value in there already or not.
cues.zh: 维护唯一索引和其他索引的工作量是一样的，反正都得插入索引。区别只在于，要是发现值已存在，它会不会报错。

cues.en: You have a question back there? Okay.
cues.zh: 后面那位有疑问？好的。

cues.en: Again, this is a huge topic, but this will, you know, get you going
cues.zh: 再次声明，这是个很大的话题，不过这些内容能帮你起步，

cues.en: because people say the query is slow.
cues.zh: 因为大家总说查询太慢了。

cues.en: So explain or explain analyze. The problem is the output is somewhat cryptic. So let... Let's look at an example here.
cues.zh: 那就是 EXPLAIN 或是 EXPLAIN ANALYZE。问题在于输出的内容有点晦涩。那……我们来看个例子。

cues.en: The first thing I encourage everyone to look at is this wonderful, wonderful website called explain.depez.com.
cues.zh: 首先我建议大家看看这个超赞的网站，叫 explain.depesz.com。

cues.en: You can cut and paste your query plan into it, and it'll give you a tabular
cues.zh: 你可以把查询计划复制粘贴进去，它会生成一个表格

cues.en: form form of it, which is really handy.
cues.zh: 形式的展示，非常实用。

cues.en: So here we have kind of your basic
cues.zh: 这里有一个很基础的

cues.en: ecommerce y kind of query.
cues.zh: 类似电商业务的查询。

cues.en: Not pretty printed. Looks horrible. Bang. And here's a query plan from it. And you go, oh my god. Here's how here's how to read these guys. It's not that bad, actually. This is a tree structure.
cues.zh: 没做格式化排版，看起来乱糟糟的。看，这是它生成的查询执行计划。你可能会惊呼“天哪”。其实看懂它们的方法是这样的，它没那么可怕。这是一个树形结构。

cues.en: Each
cues.zh: 每一个

cues.en: arrow is a leaf... Is a node of the tree.
cues.zh: 箭头都是一个叶……都是树上的一个节点。

cues.en: That's the root.
cues.zh: 那是根节点。

cues.en: So the lowest levels here are the are the ultimate leaves.
cues.zh: 所以这里的最底层就是最终的叶子节点。

cues.en: Each one of these, you can think of as a little machine that's doing something
cues.zh: 你可以把其中的每一个都看作一台小型机器，它正在做着某些事情，

cues.en: as part to execute the query.
cues.zh: 作为执行整个查询的一部分。

cues.en: For example, here are two index scans.
cues.zh: 例如，这里有两个索引扫描。

cues.en: This is an index scan
cues.zh: 这是一个索引扫描

cues.en: on
cues.zh: 在

cues.en: this index, ecommerce sold item.
cues.zh: 这个索引上，电商已售商品。

cues.en: Here's the condition it's running.
cues.zh: 这是它正在执行的条件。

cues.en: It then applies an extra filter
cues.zh: 然后它会应用一个额外的过滤器

cues.en: to throw away results from that,
cues.zh: 把不符合的结果丢掉，

cues.en: usually because of a where clause or something like that.
cues.zh: 通常是因为有 where 子句之类的。

cues.en: And then it feeds it up. This nested loop, you can think, is to execute a join. The way it works is it takes a row here.
cues.zh: 然后它把结果往上送。这个嵌套循环，你可以理解为在执行一个 join。它的工作方式是，从这里取一行。

cues.en: It says... It takes this index scan and says, okay. Here's a stream of rows coming back up from my index scan. So it's saying, Okay, I'm going to find everything with subscriber ID equals this,
cues.zh: 它说……它拿这个索引扫描说，好。这是我的索引扫描返回的一串行。所以它在说，好，我要找到所有 subscriber ID 等于这个值的记录，

cues.en: apply
cues.zh: 应用

cues.en: a filter of status, has to be any of these values. This is an array field, pretty cool.
cues.zh: 一个 status 的过滤器，必须是这些值中的任意一个。这是一个数组字段，挺酷的。

cues.en: And it hands up a row.
cues.zh: 然后它往上交出一行数据。

cues.en: And then the nested loop says, Okay, now I'm going do an index scan
cues.zh: 接着嵌套循环会说：好，现在我要做一次索引扫描了，

cues.en: based on that result. You notice you see it says e commerce ID,
cues.zh: 基于那个结果。大家注意看，这里写着电商 ID，

cues.en: e commerce order ID? So it handed up the ID here and then executed this query to do the join.
cues.zh: 电商订单 ID 对吧？所以它把这里的 ID 传了上去，然后执行这个查询来进行连接（join）。

cues.en: A nested loop always works this way, is that for every row in the... You can think of it as the top arm and the bottom arm.
cues.zh: 嵌套循环一直都是这么工作的，对于……里的每一行。你可以把它想象成上臂和下臂。

cues.en: The index
cues.zh: 索引

cues.en: feeds a row up here, and then this
cues.zh: 把一行数据往上传到这里，然后这个

cues.en: arm, which can be anything. It happens to be an index scan, this one, and then executes this one and joins them.
cues.zh: 分支，它可以是任何操作。这里刚好也是个索引扫描，然后执行它并把两者连接起来。

cues.en: And this is one of the ways Postgres does joins.
cues.zh: 这就是 Postgres 执行连接的方式之一。

cues.en: There there are other join nodes, but they all work basically the same way.
cues.zh: 还有其他连接节点，但它们的工作原理基本相同。

cues.en: It then takes the results of that and does an aggregate.
cues.zh: 接着，它会取这些结果做聚合。

cues.en: The aggregate is like a group by or a distinct or any of those clauses in SQL, where it takes a bunch of rows and smashes them down because of duplication of of a value, like group by works and, like, distinct works and things like that.
cues.zh: 聚合就像 SQL 里的 GROUP BY、DISTINCT 之类的子句：它会把一堆行合并起来，去掉重复值。GROUP BY、DISTINCT 等都是这样工作的。

cues.en: So this is what a query plan output looks like, and this is actually... You can think of this as a dump of kind of the machine language of Postgres.
cues.zh: 这就是查询计划输出的样子，其实……你可以把它看作是 Postgres 机器语言的一种转储。

cues.en: So read the execution plan from the bottom up.
cues.zh: 所以阅读执行计划要自底向上看。

cues.en: Look for nodes that are processing a lot of data,
cues.zh: 寻找那些正在处理大量数据的节点，

cues.en: especially if the data set is being reduced a lot on the way up. Those are the first places to look to optimize a query.
cues.zh: 尤其是向上流动时数据集被大幅缩减的地方。这些是优化查询的首选关注点。

cues.en: The cost for that is measured in... The cost of that cost value... Go back here. See if it's cost.
cues.zh: 其开销是用……那个 cost 值的开销……回到这里，看看是不是 cost。

cues.en: Each node has one.
cues.zh: 每个节点都有一个。

cues.en: Those are measured in arbitrary units. Traditionally, they were called disk fetches, but don't worry about them. They're just shekels. They're they're... They have no meaning.
cues.zh: 这些是用任意单位衡量的。传统上称为磁盘读取次数，但不用太在意。它们就像谢克尔一样。它们……它们没有实际意义。

cues.en: They just start for comparison to each other.
cues.zh: 它们只是为了相互比较。

cues.en: The first number is the startup cost to get the first two pullable. The second is the total cost.
cues.zh: 第一个数字是让前两个变为可拉取状态的启动成本。第二个是总成本。

cues.en: The reason you care about them is as you
cues.zh: 你关心它们的原因是，当你

cues.en: alter the query and do new ones, you can compare those, and you want the cost to go down.
cues.zh: 修改查询并执行新的查询时，可以比较这些成本，而你希望成本降低。

cues.en: One thing you have to remember is the costs are inclusive of sub nodes.
cues.zh: 有一点要记住的是，这里的开销包含了子节点的开销。

cues.en: So this cost includes all of this.
cues.zh: 所以这个开销包含了所有这些。

cues.en: So you have to do a little bit of subtraction to find out how much each node by itself costs.
cues.zh: 因此你需要做一点减法，才能算出每个节点自身的开销是多少。

cues.en: The depest.explain.com
cues.zh: depesz.explain.com

cues.en: does that for you, which is kind of nice.
cues.zh: 会帮你算好这个，这一点挺不错的。

cues.en: If you do explain analyze, it'll show you the actual time the query took in milliseconds,
cues.zh: 如果使用 EXPLAIN ANALYZE，它会显示查询实际花费的毫秒数，

cues.en: which is in wall clock time, not CPU time. So if other things are going on in the system, that can extend the values you see there.
cues.zh: 这是实际耗时，而不是 CPU 时间。所以如果系统里还有其他任务在跑，你看到的数值可能会变大。

cues.en: And it works in the same way, startup time, total time. And it's also inclusive of subnodes.
cues.zh: 它的运作方式相同，启动时间、总时间都一样，并且也包含子节点。

cues.en: Each node will tell you estimated
cues.zh: 每个节点都会告诉你预估的

cues.en: and actual rows emitted by each planner node.
cues.zh: 以及每个计划节点实际输出的行数。

cues.en: It's not the number processed. So, for example, if it filtered out a bazillion rows, it'll be the number that it produced back up, not the number it touched and threw away.
cues.zh: 它不是处理的行数。比如说，如果它过滤掉了海量行，那这里显示的是它向上返回的行数，而不是它接触过又丢弃的行数。

cues.en: One of the first places to look for is if the planner thought it would take... It would touch a small number of rows, but it really touched a large number of rows.
cues.zh: 首先要看的地方之一是：计划器是否以为它会接触少量行，但实际上它接触了大量行。

cues.en: Look the
cues.zh: 查看这个

cues.en: node,
cues.zh: 节点，

cues.en: go back to the SQL, find what part of the SQL that node was executing,
cues.zh: 回到 SQL，看看这个节点执行的是 SQL 的哪一部分，

cues.en: and
cues.zh: 然后

cues.en: see why there was a mismatch.
cues.zh: 查查看为什么不匹配。

cues.en: Bad planner statistics are one reason. You're doing a correlated query that it just got confused about, all sorts of things.
cues.zh: 规划器统计信息不准确是原因之一。比如相关子查询让它搞糊涂了，原因还有很多。

cues.en: Occasionally, you'll see a loop value, which is number of times the subplan was executed by its parent.
cues.zh: 有时你会看到一个循环次数值，表示父节点执行子计划的次数。

cues.en: Just remember, if you see this, you have to multiply the times by the number of loops cause it gives you averages.
cues.zh: 记住，看到这个值时，要把次数乘以循环数，因为这里显示的是平均值。

cues.en: Because reasons, I'm not sure why.
cues.zh: 由于种种原因吧，我也说不清为什么。

cues.en: The number one reason for queries to go bad are
cues.zh: 导致查询变慢的头号原因，

cues.en: joins between two very large tables.
cues.zh: 就是两个超大表之间的关联操作（join）。

cues.en: Unfortunately,
cues.zh: 不幸的是，

cues.en: Postgres and databases like it are so powerful, people start ascribing magical powers to them.
cues.zh: Postgres 这类数据库功能太强大了，以至于人们开始觉得它们无所不能。

cues.en: And they'll do joins between two fifty million row tables with a 10,000,000 row result and expect it to be fast.
cues.zh: 他们会把两个 5000 万行的表做关联，产生 1000 万行的结果，还指望它能跑得飞快。

cues.en: It never will be fast.
cues.zh: 这根本不可能快。

cues.en: Postgres doesn't have any magical way of making disk. Run faster.
cues.zh: Postgres 并没有什么魔法能让磁盘跑得更快。

cues.en: So joins between two very large tables are something to avoid, if at all possible.
cues.zh: 所以，两个超大表之间的连接要尽可能避免。

cues.en: The only way you can do this is
cues.zh: 要做到这一点，唯一的办法是

cues.en: if the join, one side only has to consider a very small subset of the total rows.
cues.zh: 连接时，其中一侧只需考虑总行数中很小的一部分。

cues.en: A cross join. A cross join is where you have... There's no limitation to the join. So if you join an eight row table to a 12 row table, it's gonna be eight times 12 rows come...
cues.zh: 交叉连接。交叉连接就是……连接没有任何限制。比如把一个有 8 行的表和一个有 12 行的表连接起来，结果会有 8 乘 12 行……

cues.en: Coming back.
cues.zh: 接着说。

cues.en: You rarely do these intentionally, but they're easy to do accidentally.
cues.zh: 你很少会故意这么做，但很容易不小心就这么做了。

cues.en: Another good reason that typing explain can show you that it's doing a cross join and you go, oops.
cues.zh: 另一个好理由是，输入 explain 能让你看到它在做交叉连接（cross join），这时你就会意识到“糟糕了”。

cues.en: And lastly, if it has to do a sequential scan on a large table,
cues.zh: 最后，如果它必须对一张大表进行全表顺序扫描（sequential scan），

cues.en: that's gonna be very expensive,
cues.zh: 那代价会非常高昂，

cues.en: either because there's no index that applies or you're trying to process all the rows in the table for some reason.
cues.zh: 要么是因为没有可用的索引，要么是你出于某种原因非要处理表里的所有行。

cues.en: If the planner has lost its mind,
cues.zh: 如果查询规划器（planner）失常了，

cues.en: try and do an analyze to see if you can get it... Update the statistics.
cues.zh: 试着执行一次 analyze，看看能不能……更新一下统计信息。

cues.en: Here's an example
cues.zh: 这是分析之前的一个计划。

cues.en: of a plan before an analyze.
cues.zh: 分析之前的计划示例。

cues.en: This is the one we saw earlier.
cues.zh: 这就是我们之前看到的那个。

cues.en: Then we did an analyze,
cues.zh: 然后我们做了一次分析，

cues.en: and it realized that it could generate a better plan
cues.zh: 它发现可以生成更好的计划，

cues.en: and actually cut the cost down quite a bit
cues.zh: 而且确实大幅降低了成本，

cues.en: because it understood
cues.zh: 因为它了解

cues.en: the distribution of the sold order order ID.
cues.zh: 已售订单 ID 的分布情况。

cues.en: They're collected as histograms on a per column basis,
cues.zh: 它们按列收集为直方图，

cues.en: a 100 buckets by default. They're not restored from backups, they're not automatically updated when you do major inserts and things like that. They will be eventually, but it can take a while to catch up. So if, for example, if you're doing a large bulk load or ETL process, do an analyze at the end of it.
cues.zh: 默认有 100 个桶。它们不会从备份中恢复，也不会在大量插入等操作后自动更新。之后最终会更新，但可能需要一段时间才能跟上。所以，比如说，如果你要进行大批量加载或 ETL，记得在结束时执行一次分析。

cues.en: Select count star.
cues.zh: Select count(*)。

cues.en: This always results in a full table scan in Postgres. Always, always, always.
cues.zh: 在 Postgres 中，这必定会导致全表扫描。无一例外。

cues.en: So don't do that. Don't build pagination mechanisms that require count star on a 50,000,000 row table.
cues.zh: 所以千万别这么干。别在一个有 5000 万行的表上去做依赖 count(*) 的分页。

cues.en: Offset and limit. Everybody implements offset and limit
cues.zh: Offset 和 limit。大家都会用 offset 和 limit

cues.en: to do pagination. Right? You know? Because it's obvious. They're just sitting there. You know? It's like you... You know, you're doing a forum or something like that, and you have one, two, three, four, five, six, you know, buttons down at the end.
cues.zh: 来实现分页。对吧？你懂的，因为这太直观了，现成的方法就在那。比如你做个论坛之类的，页面底部就会有 1、2、3、4、5、6 这种翻页按钮。

cues.en: And the problem is offset... If you were a CS one zero one student and you wanted to implement offset, how would you do it? They say, Oh, okay. I'll just process the query, get the result back,
cues.zh: 问题出在 offset 上……如果你是个学计算机科学导论的学生，要实现 offset，你会怎么做？他们会说：“哦，好吧。我先处理查询，拿到结果，

cues.en: and then throw away the first 100 rows if it's an offset 100.
cues.zh: 然后如果 offset 是 100，就把前 100 行丢掉。

cues.en: That's the way offset works in Postgres.
cues.zh: Postgres 里的 offset 就是这么工作的。

cues.en: It's not special.
cues.zh: 它没什么特别的。

cues.en: So
cues.zh: 所以

cues.en: it comes apart for higher problems in the...
cues.zh: 问题一大，

cues.en: You do an offset 10,000,000,
cues.zh: 如果你设置 offset 10,000,000，

cues.en: it's gonna throw away the first 10,000,000 rows,
which is very expensive. The problem here is, of course, if you have something like Googlebot going through your forum,
cues.zh: 这代价非常高。当然，问题在于，如果 Googlebot 这样的爬虫在浏览你的论坛，

cues.en: it will it will go through all 500 pages
cues.zh: 它会用 offset 翻完全部 500 页，

cues.en: doing offsets.
cues.zh: 一页一页地翻。

cues.en: So pre calculate and use other keys. Something I'll add to the slides is there's actually a really good website called use the index loop that gives alternatives for doing pagination.
cues.zh: 所以要提前计算，并使用其他键。我之后会加到幻灯片里的是，其实有一个非常棒的网站叫 Use The Index, Luke!，它提供了做分页的替代方案。

cues.en: Okay. We're almost done.
cues.zh: 好了，我们差不多快讲完了。

cues.en: Basic troubleshooting. So the database is slow. People say, hey. You're responsible for the database, and everything's slow.
cues.zh: 基本排错。假设数据库变慢了，有人找你说：“嘿，你负责这个数据库，现在所有东西都很慢。”

cues.en: You want to look at this... At p g stat activity. That's another view, select star from p g stat activity.
cues.zh: 你会想查看这个……查看 pg_stat_activity。那是另一个视图，执行 select * from pg_stat_activity 即可。

cues.en: That shows you all the processes that are going on.
cues.zh: 这会显示所有正在进行的进程。

cues.en: You can also tail the logs.
cues.zh: 你也可以跟踪日志。

cues.en: Log into the database server, go to the text logs, tail... Do a tail f. Is there, in fact, a lot of traffic on the logs? See what's going on.
cues.zh: 登录数据库服务器，进入文本日志，跟踪……执行 tail -f。日志上是不是确实有大量流量？看看发生了什么。

cues.en: I would install the sysstat package.
cues.zh: 我会安装 sysstat 包。

cues.en: You can do iostat dash x five and see if the date... If the file system... The database volume is overloaded, like the utilization's hitting a 100%,
cues.zh: 你可以执行 iostat -x 5，看看日期……看看文件系统……数据库卷是否过载，比如利用率达到 100%，

cues.en: and you're just running out of IO.
cues.zh: 而你的 IO 已经耗尽了。

cues.en: The database crashed.
cues.zh: 数据库崩溃了。

cues.en: First, make sure it really is up. You know? Can you PSQL into it? Did it actually crash?
cues.zh: 首先，确认它真的启动了。能用 PSQL 连进去吗？它真的崩溃了吗？

cues.en: And, again, look at PG stat activity and also look at PG locks.
cues.zh: 再看看 PG stat activity 和 PG locks。

cues.en: P g stat activity, which you just, you know, go in and type that,
cues.zh: PG stat activity，你只要进去输入这个，

cues.en: it shows each connected client and what they are or were doing. It will show you the last query for ones that are not currently running.
cues.zh: 它会显示每个已连接的客户端，以及它们正在做或之前做过什么。对于当前没有运行查询的客户端，它会显示最后一条查询。

cues.en: There's a column called state. If it's active, it's currently running.
cues.zh: 有一列叫 state。如果值是 active，说明查询正在运行。

cues.en: And a column called waiting, and if it's true, it's waiting to acquire a lock.
cues.zh: 还有一列叫 waiting，如果值为 true，就表示它正在等待获取锁。

cues.en: So then we bop over to p g locks.
cues.zh: 然后我们跳到 pg_locks。

cues.en: Same thing, select star from p g locks.
cues.zh: 同样，执行 select star from pg_locks。

cues.en: It shows all the locks that are currently active in the system. There's a lot of noise in this table.
cues.zh: 它会显示系统里当前所有活动的锁。这张表里有很多杂项信息。

cues.en: So don't panic if you type select star from PG locks. It comes back with 12,000 rows.
cues.zh: 所以，执行 select star from PG locks 后返回 12,000 行也不用慌。

cues.en: Don't worry about that. What you wanna look for is the granted column is false.
cues.zh: 别担心。你要找的是 granted 列值为 false 的行。

cues.en: And because that shows a lock that's been granted or that's been waited for but hasn't been granted yet.
cues.zh: 因为这能显示已经获取的锁，或者正在等待但尚未获取的锁。

cues.en: And find out who's waiting on those locks.
cues.zh: 并找出是谁在等待这些锁。

cues.en: Specifically,
cues.zh: 具体来说，

cues.en: any lock that's trying to acquire a virtual XID, don't worry about it. You'll see tons of those, and there's nothing... Those those are noise.
cues.zh: 任何试图获取虚拟 XID 的锁，都不用担心。你会看到大量的这种锁，没什么……那些都是干扰信息。

cues.en: You can also... There are also row level locks.
cues.zh: 你也可以……此外还有行级锁。

cues.en: Specific row level locks don't appear in PG stat activity or PG locks.
cues.zh: 具体的行级锁不会出现在 pg_stat_activity 或 pg_locks 中。

cues.en: For example, somebody's updated a row and somebody else is blocked waiting for that row to be updated, a very common scenario.
cues.zh: 比如，有人更新了一行，另一个人正等着这行更新完，这是很常见的情况。

cues.en: You can find those using contrib PG role locks.
cues.zh: 可以用 contrib PG 的 role locks 找到这类问题。

cues.en: It does do a sequential scan of a table, so it can take a while. A very common anti pattern
cues.zh: 它确实会顺序扫描整张表，所以可能要花点时间。一个很常见的反模式是

cues.en: is to have something like a user table with a very fast changing field in it, like last clicked,
cues.zh: 用户表里有个字段频繁更新，比如上次点击时间，

cues.en: and everybody piles up on a lock on that user row.
cues.zh: 结果所有人都堵在这条用户记录的锁上。

cues.en: Especially if, for example, you have multiple...
cues.zh: 尤其是，比如你有多个……

cues.en: You you have a typical modern application with lots of stuff running in the browser that's all accessing the same user object
cues.zh: 比如，你有一个典型的现代应用，浏览器里运行着很多东西，它们都在访问同一个用户对象

cues.en: from multiple different connections.
cues.zh: 而且来自多个不同的连接。

cues.en: A lot of these things have... Just don't display the names of tables. They display object IDs.
cues.zh: 很多这类东西……只是不显示表名，而是显示对象 ID。

cues.en: So for example, pg locks, as Colm said, the relation, and you'll see a number there.
cues.zh: 比如，正如 Colm 所说，pg_locks 里的 relation 会显示一个数字。

cues.en: You can type select and the number colon colon reg class to get the name
cues.zh: 你可以输入 select，再输入这个数字::regclass，就能查到它的名称

cues.en: of it.
And lastly, some special situations.
cues.zh: 最后，还有一些特殊情况。

cues.en: A minor version upgrade.
cues.zh: 升级次要版本。

cues.en: This... A minor version in Postgres is the last number of the three numbers. So 9199951
cues.zh: 在 Postgres 里，次要版本是三位版本号中的最后一位。所以 9199951

cues.en: to 952
is a minor version upgrade. Do these promptly.
cues.zh: 就是升级次要版本。要尽快升级。

cues.en: They're released for a reason, usually a bug in the... A bug release.
cues.zh: 它们发布自有原因，通常是为了修复程序错误……也就是错误修复版本。

cues.en: Only... The good news is it only requires installing new binaries. You don't have to do anything to the database. You just have to shut the database down and bring it back up on the new binaries.
cues.zh: 好消息是，只需要安装新的二进制文件。不用对数据库做任何操作。只要关闭数据库，再用新的二进制文件启动即可。

cues.en: If you're using packages, often just typing yum apt get upgrade will do it for you. Sometimes you're surprised when you type sudo yum up the upgrade. It shuts down your down... Your file... Your database server and brings it back up, but
cues.zh: 如果你用的是包管理器，通常直接输入 yum 或 apt-get upgrade 就能搞定。有时你可能会吃一惊，当你敲下 sudo yum update 或 upgrade 时，它会关停你的……你的文……你的数据库服务器然后重启，但是

cues.en: it is really easy. So do these promptly.
cues.zh: 这真的很简单。所以一定要及时更新。

cues.en: You know, it's... It just pains me to death when I log into a system and and they're running nine three zero
cues.zh: 讲真，每次登录系统看到还在跑 9.3.0，

cues.en: because there's no reason for that. Just do it. It takes one minute of downtime.
cues.zh: 我都感到心痛万分，因为根本没有理由不升级。赶紧升吧，也就停机一分钟的事。

cues.en: Major version upgrades, have to plan for a little more.
cues.zh: 大版本升级需要多做一些规划。

cues.en: There's a tool called p g upgrade
cues.zh: 有个工具叫 p g upgrade

cues.en: that will do an in place... That can do an in place upgrade of major versions like nine four to nine five. So you can use that. It takes a little while. I would allow, like, half an hour of downtime depending on the size of your your schema.
cues.zh: 它可以原地升级……也就是把大版本从九四升到九五。你可以用它。升级要花点时间，具体取决于 schema 的大小，我会预留半小时左右的停机时间。

cues.en: You can also do trigger based replication to do upgrades, like using Bucardo or Slony or one of those guys. But that's fairly fiddly and complicated.
cues.zh: 你也可以用基于触发器的复制来升级，比如用 Bucardo、Slony 之类的工具。不过这相当繁琐复杂。

cues.en: And you can always do a full pg dump and pg restore
cues.zh: 你也可以直接做一次完整的 pg dump，再用 pg restore 恢复

cues.en: if your database is of a size that is that's acceptable.
cues.zh: 前提是你的数据库大小在可接受的范围内。

cues.en: And that's the easiest way to always do these.
cues.zh: 这是处理这些升级最简单的办法。

cues.en: Always read the release notes because there's often some magical thing you have to do on an upgrade.
cues.zh: 一定要看发行说明，因为升级时经常有些特别的步骤要做。

cues.en: Just remember, major versions are end of life after five years. 9.1
cues.zh: 记住，主版本五年后就会停止维护。9.1

cues.en: support ends in September this year.
cues.zh: 支持会在今年九月结束。

cues.en: And always have a plan. You don't have to execute the plan immediately,
cues.zh: 一定要有计划。你不必马上执行，

cues.en: but always have a plan. Don't get stuck like my poor client with a multi terabyte database on eight two.
cues.zh: 但一定要有计划。别像我那位可怜的客户一样，数据库有好几个 TB，还在用 8.2。

cues.en: And if you have a primary and a secondary,
cues.zh: 如果你有主节点和辅助节点，

cues.en: the primary and secondary all have to be the same major version.
cues.zh: 主节点和辅助节点的主版本号都必须相同。

cues.en: So plan for the whole shebang.
cues.zh: 所以要把整套东西都规划好。

cues.en: If you do bulk data loads, use copy, not insert.
cues.zh: 如果要批量加载数据，用 COPY，不要用 INSERT。

cues.en: Copy does the whole... Does integrity checking and trigger processing, so there's no bad thing about doing copy. And remember to do a vacuum analyze afterwards to update the planner statistics.
cues.zh: COPY 会做完整性检查和触发器处理，所以用 COPY 没什么坏处。记得之后执行 VACUUM ANALYZE，更新规划器统计信息。

cues.en: If you have a very high insert rate database, and by a very high, I mean tens of thousands of inserts per second,
cues.zh: 如果你的数据库插入速率很高，我指的是每秒数万次插入，

cues.en: It's often a good idea to reduce shared buffers, but to 25%
cues.zh: 通常可以考虑调低共享缓冲区，不过调到原来的 25%

cues.en: to 75% of what they would be otherwise so the checkpoints flush faster
cues.zh: 到 75% 之间，这样检查点就能更快刷新，

cues.en: and reduce the checkpoint time out aggressively so that it stays on top of them.
cues.zh: 还要大幅缩短检查点超时时间，让它能及时跟上。

cues.en: Remember that high insert rates means the data is changing a lot, so analyze could get out of date very fast. So you may want to do manual analyzes on the high insert rate tables as well.
cues.zh: 记住，插入频率高意味着数据变化很快，所以分析结果可能很快就过时。对于插入频率高的表，你可能也需要手动执行分析。

cues.en: If you're on AWS,
cues.zh: 如果你用的是 AWS，

cues.en: generally, works like any other system.
cues.zh: 通常来说，它的运作方式和其他系统一样。

cues.en: Just remember instances can disappear and come back without their instance storage.
cues.zh: 只要记住，实例可能会消失，之后重新出现时，实例存储里的数据可能已经不在了。

cues.en: So always have a good backup and replication strategy on AWS. These servers are terrible.
cues.zh: 所以在 AWS 上一定要制定可靠的备份和复制策略。这些服务器真不怎么样。

cues.en: If you're running... If your primary database is on on
cues.zh: 如果你正在运行……如果你的主数据库部署在

cues.en: EBS,
cues.zh: EBS 上，

cues.en: Spring for PI Ops, they're expensive,
cues.zh: 尽量选预置 IOPS（PIOPS），虽然价格不菲，

cues.en: but they're
cues.zh: 但要想让

cues.en: really necessary for a reasonable performance on a database.
cues.zh: 数据库拥有像样的性能，它确实必不可少。

cues.en: If you have a big AWS employment, script everything
cues.zh: 如果你的 AWS 部署规模很大，一定要把所有操作脚本化，

cues.en: so that you don't have to go around and upgrade
cues.zh: 这样你就不必

cues.en: 23 servers
cues.zh: 一台台手动去升级

cues.en: by hand.
cues.zh: 整整 23 台服务器了。

cues.en: By all means, use a VPC. It's a much better way of managing this stuff.
cues.zh: 务必使用 VPC，管理这些资源会顺手得多。

cues.en: And just remember, AWS is really expensive as a way to rent equipment.
cues.zh: 另外要记住，把 AWS 当作租用设备的方式其实非常昂贵。

cues.en: You know, e c two stands for elastic computing.
cues.zh: 大家知道，EC2 代表的是弹性计算。

cues.en: So see if there's a way you can scale up and scale down to meet demand rather than just leave 18 database servers running all the time.
cues.zh: 所以不妨想想办法，按需弹性伸缩，而不是一直开着 18 台数据库服务器空转。

cues.en: RDS,
cues.zh: RDS，

cues.en: the new hotness for deploying Postgres.
cues.zh: 部署 Postgres 的新宠。

cues.en: Overall, it's not a bad product.
cues.zh: 总的来说，它是个不错的产品。

cues.en: The big plus is it handles automated failover between a primary and a secondary very nicely.
cues.zh: 最大的亮点在于，它能非常漂亮地处理主从节点间的自动故障转移。

cues.en: So that if the... If your primary goes down, it will... You can set up a shadow secondary.
cues.zh: 这样一来……如果你的主库宕机了，它就会……你可以配置一个备份从库。

cues.en: You can't direct any write traffic to it because it doesn't actually use Postgres streaming replication,
cues.zh: 你无法向它分发任何写入流量，因为它实际上并没有使用 Postgres 流复制，

cues.en: but
cues.zh: 但是

cues.en: it's there and it'll switch over for you. That's actually kind of a pain in the neck to do on community Postgres.
cues.zh: 它就在那里，而且会自动帮你完成故障转移。这在社区版 Postgres 里其实挺让人头疼的。

cues.en: But there's a big minus, which is
cues.zh: 但它也有个大缺点，那就是

cues.en: the performance is relatively bad compared to bare EC2.
cues.zh: 相比裸机部署在 EC2 上，它的性能相对较差。

cues.en: And the biggest problem is when the performance is bad, it's really mysterious why it's bad.
cues.zh: 而最大的问题在于，一旦性能变差，你根本搞不清它为什么会变差，简直玄学。

cues.en: Because you don't have access to the underlying instance, so there's a lot of stuff you can't figure out as to what's going on.
cues.zh: 因为你访问不到底层实例，所以有很多东西你没法弄清楚到底发生了什么。

cues.en: It's expensive compared to bare EC2.
cues.zh: 跟裸 EC2 相比，它很贵。

cues.en: And you have a fixed set of extensions.
cues.zh: 而且你只能用固定的一组扩展。

cues.en: It's a relatively large and good set of extensions, but they are fixed.
cues.zh: 这组扩展相对比较大、也比较好，但它们是固定的。

cues.en: However, that all being said, if you're just getting started, it's not a bad place to start.
cues.zh: 不过话说回来，如果你才刚起步，从这里开始也不算差。

cues.en: So good place to be going for.
cues.zh: 所以是个不错的起点。

cues.en: Sharding.
cues.zh: 分片。

cues.en: The number one place that you run out of capacity on Postgres is
cues.zh: Postgres 最先遇到的容量瓶颈是

cues.en: write capacity on the master.
cues.zh: 主节点的写入能力。

cues.en: So what do you do?
cues.zh: 那该怎么办？

cues.en: Right now, community PostgresQL doesn't have an integrated multi master solution. There are some options.
cues.zh: 目前，社区版 PostgreSQL 没有集成的多主节点方案，不过还有一些选择。

cues.en: One thing to look at is Postgres XC,
cues.zh: 可以看看 Postgres XC，

cues.en: which is an open source
cues.zh: 它是一个开源的

cues.en: fork, I can't talk, of Postgres. It's intended for dedicated hardware in a single rack.
cues.zh: 分支——我这都说不利索了。它面向单个机架中的专用硬件。

cues.en: So node failure is still kind of a challenge. It's not great in a cloud hosting environment.
cues.zh: 所以节点故障仍然是个难题。它不太适合云托管环境。

cues.en: But it's somewhat experimental, but it's pretty interesting.
cues.zh: 不过它还比较实验性，但挺有意思的。

cues.en: There's a commercial product with an open source variant called CitusDB,
cues.zh: 有一款商业产品，还有一个叫 CitusDB 的开源版本，

cues.en: which is... It used to be a fork, now it's actually an extension that you can install. There's an open source for... It's, you know,
cues.zh: 它以前是一个分支，现在其实是可以安装的扩展。它是开源的……你知道，

cues.en: hybrid open source commercial model.
cues.zh: 采用开源与商业结合的模式。

cues.en: It's really good for data... It's it's intended mostly for data warehousing kind of situations,
cues.zh: 它很适合处理数据……主要是用于数据仓库这类场景，

cues.en: and it does column or store data. And it's pretty cool.
cues.zh: 而且它以列式存储数据，挺不错的。

cues.en: It's not super simple, but if you're doing a data warehouse kind of thing and you want sharding to help improve stuff, it's a good choice.
cues.zh: 这并不算特别简单，不过如果你在做数据仓库这类项目，想用分片来提升性能，那它是个不错的选择。

cues.en: Again,
cues.zh: 再说一次，

cues.en: Vucardo is your choice, right now your only solution for true multi master write.
cues.zh: Vucardo 是你的选择。目前它是实现真正多主写入的唯一方案。

cues.en: It's good for burst writes. The problem is on sustained writes, of course, ultimately it has to bring everything back up to date.
cues.zh: 它适合突发写入。当然，持续写入的问题在于，最终它得把所有数据都同步到最新状态。

cues.en: So it won't it won't help you for sustained write load. But if one side gets a burst, that can be helpful.
cues.zh: 所以它对持续写入负载没什么帮助。不过如果一边出现突发写入，它就能派上用场。

cues.en: Or you can build custom sharding
cues.zh: 或者你也可以在应用层

cues.en: in the application.
cues.zh: 实现自定义分片。

cues.en: The the problem is, of course, the application has to do this, which can be complicated.
cues.zh: 当然，问题在于应用层必须承担这部分逻辑，这可能会很复杂。

cues.en: There's a tech note that Instagram wrote on how they did... Do they do their sharding. At least they used to.
cues.zh: Instagram 曾写过一篇技术随笔，讲他们是如何做分片的。至少他们以前是这么做的。

cues.en: Lastly,
cues.zh: 最后，

cues.en: pooling.
cues.zh: 连接池。

cues.en: Opening a connection to Postgres is expensive.
cues.zh: 在 Postgres 中建立连接开销很大。

cues.en: It can actually be longer than the query time.
cues.zh: 耗时甚至可能比实际查询还要长。

cues.en: So
cues.zh: 所以，

cues.en: if have
cues.zh: 如果连接数

cues.en: more than 200 to 300 connections, use a pooler.
cues.zh: 超过两三百个，就一定要用连接池工具。

cues.en: The pooler you probably want to use is pgbouncer.
cues.zh: 你最可能想用的连接池工具是 pgbouncer。

cues.en: It's developed by Skype. It's really easy to install, and it's very fast and can handle thousands of connections.
cues.zh: 它由 Skype 开发，安装非常简单，速度极快，还能处理数千个连接。

cues.en: One of the problems, it doesn't do failover or load balancing at all. It's intended to be in front of a single server.
cues.zh: 但有个问题，它完全不支持故障转移或负载均衡，设计初衷就是放在单台服务器前面使用的。

cues.en: If you want that kind of stuff, you can use HAProxy.
cues.zh: 如果你需要这些功能，可以使用 HAProxy。

cues.en: There is a tool called pgpool2 that does query analysis, so it can route queries between primaries and secondaries
cues.zh: 还有一个叫 pgpool2 的工具，它可以做查询分析，进而把查询路由到主库或从库，

cues.en: based on whether it's read or write traffic, which is super cool.
cues.zh: 依据是读流量还是写流量来分发，这功能超级酷。

cues.en: It does load balancing and failover and secondary promotion and all this stuff. It is higher overhead, and it is more complicated to set up.
cues.zh: 它能做负载均衡、故障转移、提升备用节点，还有很多其他功能。但它开销更大，配置也更复杂。

cues.en: And some tools.
cues.zh: 还有一些工具。

cues.en: Monitor, monitor, monitor. Please monitor your database.
cues.zh: 监控，监控，再监控。请监控你的数据库。

cues.en: At the minimum, monitor disk space. There's a lot of failures. The very, very first thing you find out about is disk space is going up.
cues.zh: 至少要监控磁盘空间。很多故障都是从磁盘空间不断增长开始的，这是你最先会发现的问题。

cues.en: Monitor CPU usage
cues.zh: 监控 CPU 使用率

cues.en: and memory usage.
cues.zh: 和内存使用情况。

cues.en: Monitor replication lag.
cues.zh: 监控复制延迟。

cues.en: If the secondary disconnects,
cues.zh: 如果备用节点断开了，

cues.en: you want to know about it, and the first way you'll probably know about this is replication lag starts going up.
cues.zh: 你需要知道这件事，而你最先发现的，很可能是复制延迟开始上升。

cues.en: If you're using Nagios,
cues.zh: 如果你在用 Nagios，

cues.en: there's a plug in called checkpostgres.pl
cues.zh: 有个插件叫 checkpostgres.pl

cues.en: that you can get from buccardo.org
cues.zh: 可以从 buccardo.org 获取，

cues.en: that will check for things like replication lag and stuff like that. And plugs into NPR. It's an NPRE plug in, so you plug into whatever you want.
cues.zh: 它能检查复制延迟之类的指标，还能接入 NPR。它是个 NPRE 插件，可以接入你想接的任何东西。

cues.en: If you don't like pg...
cues.zh: 如果你不喜欢 pg…

cues.en: PSQL, there's pgadmin three, which is a graphical
cues.zh: PSQL 有 pgAdmin 3，它是一个图形化

cues.en: UI
cues.zh: 界面

cues.en: for running queries and things like that. It's pretty nice.
cues.zh: 用来执行查询之类的操作。挺好用的。

cues.en: I like NaviCat for general database things, but it's commercial product.
cues.zh: 我喜欢用 NaviCat 做通用数据库管理，但它是商业产品。

cues.en: I suggest everybody who's running a database that kind of matters, you know, there's revenue attached to it. There's a tool called PG Badger.
cues.zh: 我建议所有运行重要数据库的人——你知道，就是有收入挂钩的那种——都用用 PG Badger 这个工具。

cues.en: It's a long story why it's called PG Badger.
cues.zh: 它为什么叫 PG Badger，说来话长。

cues.en: It's the... It it takes the text logs and processes them and generates a nice HTML report from them so you don't have to grep through logs for all sorts of things. So I suggest installing that.
cues.zh: 它会……它把文本日志拿来处理，生成一份漂亮的 HTML 报告，这样你就不用去日志里 grep 各种东西了。所以我建议装上它。

cues.en: There's also an extension you can drop into Postgres called pgstatstatements
cues.zh: 另外，你可以在 Postgres 里安装一个叫 pgstatstatements 的扩展

cues.en: that collect
cues.zh: 用来收集

cues.en: statistics about commonly used queries and how often they were run and things like that. It's very handy.
cues.zh: 常用查询的统计信息，比如它们的执行频率之类的。非常方便。

cues.en: I mean...
cues.zh: 我是说……

cues.en: And that's everything. Questions?
cues.zh: 就这些。有什么问题吗？

cues.en: Yes, sir.
cues.zh: 有，先生。

cues.en: This is just Memcached, right? And I'm sorry, what's the problem Memcached is having?
cues.zh: 这不就是 Memcached 吗？不好意思，Memcached 有什么问题？

cues.en: Well,
cues.zh: 嗯，

cues.en: there's nothing in Postgres that automatically
cues.zh: Postgres 里没有任何东西能自动

cues.en: interacts with Memcached.
cues.zh: 和 Memcached 交互。

cues.en: So that would be an application y kind of thing for figuring out what your caching strategy is there.
cues.zh: 所以那会是一种应用层面的东西，用来搞清楚你那里的缓存策略是什么。

cues.en: So
cues.zh: 所以

cues.en: pg pool itself doesn't automatically cache queries or anything like that. It just picks them up and pass them on
cues.zh: pg pool 本身不会自动缓存查询之类的。它只是接收查询然后转发出去

cues.en: to Postgres.
cues.zh: 到 Postgres。

cues.en: So,
cues.zh: 所以，

cues.en: you know, that strategy is a common one where you have some kind of front end cache so you don't have to hit the database if you don't need to. But I'd have to see what was actually being implemented there.
cues.zh: 你知道，那种策略很常见，就是有个前端缓存，这样不需要的时候就不用去访问数据库。但我得看看那里实际实现的是什么。

cues.en: This is the feedback link.
cues.zh: 这是反馈链接。

cues.en: I will give people a moment to grab it
cues.zh: 我留点时间给大家保存一下，

cues.en: in case there's a delay in my getting the slides up. And I would always appreciate feedback.
cues.zh: 免得我切幻灯片的时候有人没赶上。非常欢迎大家提意见。

cues.en: That's my company. Hire us to do stuff.
cues.zh: 这是我的公司，欢迎找我们合作。

cues.en: And thank you.
cues.zh: 谢谢大家。

cues.en: I'm sorry? Oh, yes.
cues.zh: 什么？哦，好的。

cues.en: I'll just leave this up for a moment while people pack up.
cues.zh: 大家收拾东西的时候，我就先把这个页面放着。
